It achieves top performance on current-event and historical-memory commentary tracks with bounded computation.
AI.motivation: Streaming video understanding requires causal state updates and semantic organization of growing history under bounded computation, which is especially challenging for live soccer commentary where the system must describe events, summarize play, recall earlier moments, or stay silent based only on past information.
AI.method: StreamSoccer uses event memory as its intermediate representation. A fixed-budget active memory integrates the incoming stream; completed event states are retained locally and consolidated into retrievable historical records. A unified generator produces three commentary modes from current, recent, and historical context, while a rule-assisted scheduler selects a mode or silence. A three-track streaming soccer commentary dataset and layered evaluation protocol are constructed.
AI.result: StreamSoccer achieves CIDEr scores of 38.62, 23.96, and 17.39 for current-event, recent-window, and historical-memory commentary, ranking first on current-event and historical-memory tracks and second on recent-window. Ablations show local completed events improve all tracks. Per-minute RTF p95 ranges from 0.10 to 0.22 across 174 raw-video runs without sustained growth with match history.
AI.conclusion: Event memory effectively supports streaming soccer commentary across temporal scopes while controlling long-history computation, demonstrating that explicitly modeling event lifecycles is a viable alternative to frame-, token-, or cache-centric streaming video-language models.

title: TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in video understanding and reasoning. Despite extensive studies on text- and image-based jailbreaks, video jailbreaks against LVLMs remain largely unexplored. Existing video jailbreak methods mainly manipulate textual content embedded in videos, while overlooking how such information is organized over time. Our analysis reveals that jailbreak effectiveness depends not only on the semantics of textual information but also on its temporal presentation, including duration and timing-slot allocation. Motivated by this finding, we use subtitles, which are common in real-world videos and allow semantic content to be presented under precise temporal control without appearing visually intrusive, as a natural attack medium. Based on this insight, we propose TempJail, a black-box video-based jailbreak framework that constructs query-aligned dialogue-style subtitle sequences and optimizes their temporal scheduling to exploit temporal vulnerabilities in LVLMs and elicit responses that satisfy the harmful intent of the source query. Extensive experiments on four representative LVLMs and two datasets demonstrate that TempJail achieves the highest attack success rate across all evaluated model--dataset settings, outperforming the strongest baseline by 53 and 18 percentage points in dataset-averaged ASR on GPT-5 and Gemini 3.5-Flash, respectively.

AI.tldr: TempJail is a black-box video jailbreak framework that exploits temporal vulnerabilities in large vision-language models (LVLMs) by using subtitles with optimized temporal scheduling to elicit harmful responses, achieving state-of-the-art attack success rates on four LVLMs and two datasets.
AI.motivation: Video jailbreaks against LVLMs remain largely unexplored compared to text- and image-based attacks. Existing video jailbreak methods only manipulate textual content embedded in videos but overlook how information is organized over time. The authors discover that jailbreak effectiveness depends on temporal presentation (duration and timing-slot allocation), not just semantics.
AI.method: TempJail constructs query-aligned dialogue-style subtitle sequences as the attack medium (since subtitles allow precise temporal control without visual intrusiveness) and optimizes their temporal scheduling to exploit temporal vulnerabilities in LVLMs, eliciting responses that satisfy the harmful intent of the source query.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on four representative LVLMs and two datasets show TempJail achieves the highest attack success rate across all evaluated model-dataset settings, outperforming the strongest baseline by 53 and 18 percentage points in dataset-averaged ASR on GPT-5 and Gemini 3.5-Flash, respectively.
AI.conclusion: Temporal presentation of harmful content in videos is a critical but previously overlooked dimension for jailbreaking LVLMs. TempJail demonstrates that temporal scheduling of subtitles can effectively bypass safety mechanisms in state-of-the-art LVLMs, revealing a new attack surface that warrants further defense research.

title: Learning to Beat: Phenotype-Guided Latent Flow with Regional Motion Priors for Biventricular Motion Synthesis
summary: Full-cycle biventricular geometry is essential for characterizing cardiac function. However, dense and temporally consistent 3D+t biventricular meshes are not routinely available, whereas end-diastolic (ED) anatomy can often be obtained reliably. We therefore investigate full-cycle biventricular motion synthesis from a single ED mesh. This task is challenging because cardiac deformation is spatially heterogeneous and phenotype dependent, while conventional global generative models often obscure localized motion patterns. In this study, we propose a region-specific and phenotype-adaptive framework that integrates motion-informed functional parcellation with conditional latent flow. A functional partition learned from reconstructed motion organizes the ventricular surface into regions with coherent dynamics and enables topology-aware regional feature exchange. A phenotype-conditioned rectified-flow model subsequently maps the ED anatomy to full-cycle motion latents through fine-grained conditioning and prototype-routed motion adapters. An optional control branch further incorporates available motion descriptors for controllable synthesis. Experiments on ACDC, M\&Ms, and M\&Ms-2 demonstrate consistent improvements in geometric accuracy and functional fidelity. Under ED-only synthesis, our method achieves biventricular ASSD, HD95, and vRMSE of \(1.49\pm0.34\)~mm, \(3.77\pm1.06\)~mm, and \(3.31\pm1.03\)~mm, respectively, outperforming all competing methods. Complementary functional and robustness evaluations further demonstrate that the synthesized sequences preserve physiologically plausible ventricular dynamics and generalize across cohorts and disease phenotypes. The code will be released publicly upon acceptance of the manuscript for publication.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a region-specific and phenotype-adaptive framework for synthesizing full-cycle biventricular cardiac motion from a single end-diastolic (ED) mesh, using motion-informed functional parcellation combined with a phenotype-conditioned rectified-flow model. The method achieves state-of-the-art geometric accuracy and functional fidelity on ACDC, M&Ms, and M&Ms-2 datasets.
AI.motivation: Full-cycle biventricular geometry is essential for cardiac function assessment, but dense and temporally consistent 3D+t meshes are not routinely available, whereas ED anatomy can often be obtained reliably. Existing global generative models struggle because cardiac deformation is spatially heterogeneous and phenotype dependent, often obscuring localized motion patterns.
AI.method: The framework consists of: (1) a functional partition learned from reconstructed motion that organizes the ventricular surface into regions with coherent dynamics and enables topology-aware regional feature exchange; (2) a phenotype-conditioned rectified-flow model mapping ED anatomy to full-cycle motion latents via fine-grained conditioning and prototype-routed motion adapters; (3) an optional control branch incorporating available motion descriptors for controllable synthesis.
AI.result: The method achieves biventricular ASSD of 1.49±0.34 mm, HD95 of 3.77±1.06 mm, and vRMSE of 3.31±1.03 mm under ED-only synthesis, outperforming all competing methods on ACDC, M&Ms, and M&Ms-2 datasets with consistent improvements in geometric accuracy and functional fidelity.
AI.conclusion: The synthesized sequences preserve physiologically plausible ventricular dynamics and generalize across cohorts and disease phenotypes. The code will be released publicly upon acceptance.

title: Question-Guided Evidence Acquisition for Multimodal Visual Question Answering
summary: Multimodal LLMs can see a document, but they often can't read it reliably. Small text, tables, visual cues, and topological elements still trip them up under direct visual inference, even when the page is already sitting in the model's context. Most document-VQA systems treat perception as fixed: they encode the page once, ask the question, and answer from whatever the model happened to extract in that single fast pass. We think document VQA needs slower, more deliberate perception: rather than answering from one fixed encoding, the model should spend a bit of extra compute at inference time working out what to look at next, and only then answer. We build this into \textbf{Q-Guide}, a small agent that reads a question, works out what evidence it is still missing, and calls targeted tool(s) to recover it---reading text where text is needed, zooming in where detail is needed, or grounding a region where position matters. On DocVQA2026 and Manga109, Q-Guide outperforms both direct prompting and recent multi-agent document systems ($65.0\%$ vs.\ $40.0\%$ on DocVQA2026, $32.4\%$ vs.\ $24.4\%$ on Manga109), and the improvement holds across three Claude backbones (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, and Opus 4.5). We find that accuracy scales with the perception budget---most of the gain appears within two to three deliberate rounds---and that the gain comes from directing perception to the right place, not from complex control logic: adding planners, routers, or multiple collaborating agents does not help.

AI.tldr: Q-Guide is a small agent-based system for document VQA that performs deliberate, iterative perception at inference time—reading text, zooming into details, or grounding regions as needed—outperforming direct prompting and multi-agent baselines on DocVQA2026 (65.0% vs 40.0%) and Manga109 (32.4% vs 24.4%) across multiple Claude backbones.
AI.motivation: Multimodal LLMs struggle to reliably read documents (small text, tables, visual cues, topological elements) under direct visual inference. Existing document-VQA systems treat perception as fixed—encoding the page once and answering in a single pass—which limits accuracy. The authors argue that document VQA needs slower, more deliberate perception that guides what to look at next.
AI.method: Q-Guide is a small agent that reads the question, determines what evidence is still missing, and calls targeted tools to recover it: reading text, zooming into regions, or grounding spatial positions. It uses iterative rounds of perception before answering, allocating extra compute at inference time.
AI.result: Q-Guide outperforms direct prompting and recent multi-agent systems: 65.0% vs 40.0% on DocVQA2026 and 32.4% vs 24.4% on Manga109. Improvements hold across three Claude backbones (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.5). Accuracy scales with perception budget, with most gains within 2–3 deliberate rounds. Gains come from directing perception to the right place, not complex control logic—planners, routers, or collaborating agents do not help.
AI.conclusion: Deliberate, targeted perception—spending extra inference-time compute on deciding what to look at next—significantly improves document VQA accuracy. Simple tool-augmented agents that direct perception to the right place are more effective than complex multi-agent control architectures.

title: Gallileo-4D: Frozen Backbone Ensemble for Dynamic 4D Reconstruction
comment: Technical report for the PhysAI Dynamic 4D Reconstruction Challenge at the ECCV 2026 Workshop on Physical AI. Third of 27 teams. 14 pages, 10 figures. Code: https://github.com/odaxai/Gallileo-4D Weights: https://huggingface.co/OdaxAI/gallileo-4d-weights
summary: We describe our entry to the PhysAI Dynamic 4D Reconstruction Challenge, which placed third of 27 teams at 0.58356 APD on the final leaderboard, without a single gradient update. This was not the plan: of thirteen fine-tuning configurations of a pre-trained 4D backbone, twelve degraded the challenge score, and eleven of those twelve improved local validation at the same time. We trace this inversion to the structure of the benchmark: only 25% of the evaluation set belongs to the data variant released for training, so updates that fit the available data damage the pre-trained features the remaining 75% relies on. Our system therefore freezes the backbone and spends its budget at inference time, fusing three decoding configurations -- temporal stride-3, horizontal-flip test-time augmentation, and dense stride-1 -- under a convex weighting. The ensemble recovers +0.041 APD over the frozen baseline, more than any training run achieved, at zero training cost.

AI.tldr: A third-place entry to the PhysAI Dynamic 4D Reconstruction Challenge (0.58356 APD) that freezes a pre-trained 4D backbone and fuses three decoding configurations via convex weighting at inference time, achieving +0.041 APD over the frozen baseline with zero gradient updates.
AI.motivation: The authors discover that fine-tuning a pre-trained 4D backbone consistently improves local validation scores while degrading the actual challenge score, due to a benchmark structure where only 25% of the evaluation set matches the released training data variant. This inversion motivates abandoning training entirely and investing all computational budget in inference-time strategies.
AI.method: The system freezes the pre-trained 4D backbone and fuses three decoding configurations at inference time: temporal stride-3, horizontal-flip test-time augmentation, and dense stride-1, combined under a convex weighting scheme. No gradient updates are performed.
AI.result: The ensemble achieved third place among 27 teams with 0.58356 APD, improving +0.041 APD over the frozen baseline—a gain exceeding that of any training run, at zero training cost.
AI.conclusion: When benchmark evaluation distributions heavily diverge from training distributions, inference-time ensembling of frozen pre-trained features can outperform fine-tuning, both in score and cost-effectiveness. The paper highlights the importance of understanding benchmark structure before choosing a training strategy.

title: Far from the Crowd: Scalable Self-Supervised Learning via Geographic Isolation
summary: Self-supervised pretraining on remote sensing imagery typically treats all samples as equally informative, despite large variability in geographic and visual structure. We propose a curriculum learning strategy for self-supervised Earth observation that ranks samples by geographic isolation, a label-free proxy derived entirely from geolocation metadata already present in geospatial datasets, requiring no image decoding, no model feedback, and no manual annotation. Unlike visual complexity proxies, it scales as O(D log D) with dataset size D and is well-defined for both contrastive and reconstructive objectives. We integrate the proposed measure into MoCoV2 and MAE pretraining and evaluate across three downstream tasks from CopernicusBench (BigEarthNet, DFC-2020, LCZ). Our curriculum reaches baseline final-epoch performance using as few as 20% of the training budget (MAE) and at most 40% (MoCo) of the training budget, and improves final downstream performance by up to +5 mAP on BigEarthNet, with gains of 1-5 points across benchmarks, matching visual-complexity curricula while reducing pre-computation cost by more than 140x (4 s vs. 568 s on SSL4EO). A CKA and effective-rank analysis further reveals that curriculum-trained encoders develop higher-dimensional, more uniformly utilized embedding spaces throughout training.

AI.tldr: A curriculum learning strategy for self-supervised Earth observation that ranks samples by geographic isolation—a label-free proxy derived from geolocation metadata—enables faster convergence and improved downstream performance across contrastive (MoCoV2) and reconstructive (MAE) pretraining, while reducing pre-computation cost by over 140x compared to visual-complexity curricula.
AI.motivation: Self-supervised pretraining on remote sensing imagery treats all samples as equally informative despite large variability in geographic and visual structure. Existing sample-ranking approaches rely on visual complexity proxies that require image decoding and model feedback, are computationally expensive, and are not well-defined for all self-supervised objectives. A label-free, scalable, and objective-agnostic curriculum signal is needed.
AI.method: The authors propose ranking samples by geographic isolation, a proxy derived purely from geolocation metadata (no image decoding, no model feedback, no manual annotation). The measure scales as O(D log D) with dataset size. They integrate this curriculum into MoCoV2 (contrastive) and MAE (reconstructive) pretraining and evaluate on three tasks from CopernicusBench (BigEarthNet, DFC-2020, LCZ). They also analyze learned representations using CKA and effective-rank metrics.
AI.result: The curriculum reaches baseline final-epoch performance using as few as 20% (MAE) and at most 40% (MoCo) of the training budget. Final downstream performance improves by up to +5 mAP on BigEarthNet, with 1-5 point gains across benchmarks, matching visual-complexity curricula while reducing pre-computation cost by more than 140x (4 s vs. 568 s on SSL4EO). CKA and effective-rank analysis shows curriculum-trained encoders develop higher-dimensional, more uniformly utilized embedding spaces.
AI.conclusion: Geographic isolation is an effective, cheap, and scalable curriculum signal for self-supervised Earth observation pretraining, achieving faster convergence and better final performance than uniform training while matching visual-complexity curricula at a fraction of the computational cost. The approach also yields more informative and uniformly utilized embedding spaces.

title: Coupled Optimal Transport with Landmark Constraints
summary: Existing optimal transport (OT) models primarily seek an OT map or plan between distributions by minimizing a prescribed transport cost or distortion. However, minimizing transport cost or distortion alone may fail to identify a geometrically meaningful transformation between the two distributions. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel coupled OT framework that leverages a small number of annotated landmarks to guide the recovery of an underlying deformation governing the distribution transformation. The coupled OT framework integrates the optimization of the transport plan and the deformation field into a unified model, where the landmark-guided deformation field and the cost-driven transport plan are coupled through a mutual-consistency constraint. As a result, the deformation is jointly determined by the annotated landmarks and cost-driven distribution matching. The proposed framework provides a principled connection between landmark-based registration and transport-based distribution matching, enabling the recovery of transport maps from sparse geometric supervision. We establish the well-definedness of the proposed model in a general variational setting and develop a finite-element-based numerical algorithm for computation whose convergence properties are systematically analyzed. The practical effectiveness of the proposed approach is verified in shape matching.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel coupled optimal transport (OT) framework that uses a small number of annotated landmarks to guide the recovery of an underlying deformation governing distribution transformation, integrating transport plan optimization and deformation field into a unified model with a mutual-consistency constraint.
AI.motivation: Existing OT models minimize a prescribed transport cost or distortion, which alone may fail to identify a geometrically meaningful transformation between two distributions. The paper aims to address this limitation by leveraging sparse geometric supervision (landmarks) to recover meaningful deformations.
AI.method: A coupled OT framework that unifies transport plan optimization and deformation field estimation through a mutual-consistency constraint. The framework includes landmark-guided deformation and cost-driven transport plan, with well-definedness established in a general variational setting, and a finite-element-based numerical algorithm with convergence analysis.
AI.result: The proposed framework provides a principled connection between landmark-based registration and transport-based distribution matching, enabling recovery of transport maps from sparse geometric supervision. Practical effectiveness is verified in shape matching.
AI.conclusion: The coupled OT framework successfully bridges landmark-based registration and OT-based distribution matching, allowing geometrically meaningful deformations to be recovered from minimal annotated landmarks, with theoretical guarantees and demonstrated utility in shape matching.

title: Core-KAN: Continuous Vision Kernels with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
summary: Conventional convolutional kernels are typically defined on fixed discrete grids, limiting their ability to accommodate heterogeneous local structures. Existing adaptive operators improve flexibility but often couple geometric scale variation with content-dependent filtering, while incurring high computational cost from per-location kernel generation. To decouple geometric scale adaptation from content-dependent filtering while avoiding expensive per-location kernel generation, we propose Continuous Relative-scale KAN (Core-KAN), a relative-scale-conditioned continuous convolution operator. Core-KAN maps input features into a compact latent basis space and uses a lightweight scale controller to predict local scales relative to an exponential moving average reference. A KAN-based generator represents depth-wise kernel bases as continuous coordinate functions, allowing the operator to synthesize spatial filters at arbitrary resolutions rather than being confined to a fixed lattice. Instead of synthesizing independent kernels at every location, it constructs a compact bank of scale-conditioned kernel responses and interpolates them according to the predicted local scale map. An independent mixing controller further combines the interpolated basis responses based on local content, explicitly decoupling geometric scale adaptation from content-dependent filtering. Together with lightweight pointwise projections, this design forms a low-rank dynamic convolution that scales efficiently with kernel size and integrates readily into hierarchical vision backbones. Experiments across three representative vision tasks show Core-KAN consistently outperforms strong convolutional and dynamic-kernel baselines with only marginal parameter and computational overhead, offering an efficient, general framework for continuous, scale-adaptive convolution.

AI.tldr: Core-KAN is a continuous, scale-adaptive convolution operator that decouples geometric scale adaptation from content-dependent filtering using a KAN-based kernel generator, achieving strong performance across vision tasks with minimal overhead.
AI.motivation: Conventional convolutions are limited by fixed discrete grids and cannot handle heterogeneous local structures. Existing adaptive operators either couple geometric scale variation with content filtering or incur high computational cost from per-location kernel generation.
AI.method: Core-KAN maps features into a compact latent basis space, uses a lightweight scale controller to predict local scales relative to an EMA reference, and employs a KAN-based generator to produce depth-wise kernel bases as continuous coordinate functions. It constructs a compact bank of scale-conditioned kernel responses and interpolates them by predicted local scale, while a separate mixing controller handles content-dependent filtering, explicitly decoupling the two. Combined with pointwise projections, this forms a low-rank dynamic convolution.
AI.result: Experiments across three representative vision tasks show Core-KAN consistently outperforms strong convolutional and dynamic-kernel baselines with only marginal parameter and computational overhead.
AI.conclusion: Core-KAN offers an efficient, general framework for continuous, scale-adaptive convolution that scales well with kernel size and integrates readily into hierarchical vision backbones.

title: Towards Clinically Faithful Medical Image Captioning via Enhanced Vision-Language Alignment
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables. Preprint submitted to IEEE for possible publication
summary: Medical image captioning is a technique that accelerates early-stage diagnostic workflows and enhances the interpretability of medical diagnostic AI systems. However, unlike general image captioning, clinically reliable captioning remains challenging due to grayscale-based modalities, subtle anatomical cues, specialized medical phrasing, and variations in data quality. Despite recent advances in large vision-language models, fluent outputs do not necessarily guarantee sufficient alignment with clinical concept spaces or evaluation criteria. To address this issue, we propose a framework that strengthens clinical alignment by separating and enhancing training-time alignment and inference-time alignment. We build a medical image captioning pipeline that integrates single/dual vision encoders based on BioMedCLIP and SigLIP2, a Q-Former, and a LLaMA-based decoder, and examine the contribution of auxiliary learning for UMLS concept/type prediction. At inference, we apply single-embedding-based reranking to select the best caption among candidates, while at training we introduce MedPAIR-SCST, which combines clinically relevant rewards to shift the generative distribution toward improved clinical alignment. Our experiments show that complementary visual representations with a multi-encoder design and concept-level auxiliary learning help preserve clinically meaningful information. Furthermore, inference-time reranking provides a practical way to improve semantic and clinical alignment without additional training, whereas MedPAIR-SCST goes beyond selection by directly improving the model's distribution to generate more consistent and clinically grounded captions. These findings suggest that jointly leveraging selection-based alignment and reinforcement-learning-based alignment can promote more trustworthy medical image captioning even in data-constrained settings.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a medical image captioning framework that strengthens clinical alignment through both training-time and inference-time techniques, using a multi-encoder architecture (BioMedCLIP and SigLIP2) with a Q-Former and LLaMA decoder, plus UMLS concept prediction auxiliary learning, inference-time reranking, and MedPAIR-SCST reinforcement learning to improve clinical reliability.
AI.motivation: Clinically reliable medical image captioning remains challenging due to grayscale modalities, subtle anatomical cues, specialized medical phrasing, and data quality variations. Large vision-language models produce fluent outputs that do not necessarily align with clinical concept spaces or evaluation criteria.
AI.method: The framework separates training-time and inference-time alignment. It uses a pipeline with single/dual vision encoders based on BioMedCLIP and SigLIP2, a Q-Former, and a LLaMA-based decoder. At training, auxiliary learning for UMLS concept/type prediction and MedPAIR-SCST with clinically relevant rewards are applied. At inference, single-embedding-based reranking selects the best caption among candidates.
AI.result: Multi-encoder design with complementary visual representations and concept-level auxiliary learning preserve clinically meaningful information. Inference-time reranking improves semantic and clinical alignment without additional training. MedPAIR-SCST goes beyond selection by directly improving the model's generative distribution for more consistent and clinically grounded captions.
AI.conclusion: Jointly leveraging selection-based alignment and reinforcement-learning-based alignment can promote more trustworthy medical image captioning even in data-constrained settings.

title: AutoLumNet: Monotone Optimal Transport for Single-Shot Exposure Correction
summary: Single-shot exposure correction aims to map an arbitrarily degraded image---whether under-exposed, over-exposed, or a spatial mixture of both---to a well-exposed output from a single capture. We present AutoLumNet, a framework that decomposes this task into a global monotone tone curve and a bounded local residual, making the global component the locus of formal guarantees. The tone curve is parameterized as the normalized cumulative integral of a strictly positive density, ensuring strict monotonicity by construction rather than by penalty. We prove that this parameterization (i)~preserves the pairwise luminance ordering of all pixels and all spatial extrema unconditionally, and (ii)~is dense in the space of valid tone corrections, containing the one-dimensional optimal-transport map from the input to any target luminance distribution. A differentiable sorted-sample Wasserstein-2 objective drives the learned curve toward the OT optimum during training. Spatially varying effects that the global map provably cannot address---local shading, chrominance shifts, and clipped-region restoration---are handled by a bounded residual decoder with dual-branch convex fusion, for which we provide an explicit sufficient condition for local order preservation. Experiments on five benchmarks (MSEC, SICE, LCDP, LOL-v1, LOL-v2-real) show that AutoLumNet achieves state-of-the-art PSNR and SSIM across both under- and over-exposure regimes at 11.2\,ms per frame, and generalizes zero-shot to pure low-light benchmarks without retraining. To our knowledge, AutoLumNet is the first exposure-correction method to unite structural monotonicity, optimal-transport optimality, and bounded local adaptivity within a single trainable architecture. Code is available at https://github.com/kraihan/Autolumnet.

AI.tldr: AutoLumNet is a single-shot exposure correction framework that decomposes the task into a globally monotone tone curve (parameterized as a normalized cumulative integral of a positive density) and a bounded local residual decoder with dual-branch convex fusion. It provably preserves luminance ordering, is dense in the space of valid tone corrections containing the OT map, uses a differentiable sorted-sample Wasserstein-2 objective, and achieves SOTA PSNR/SSIM on five benchmarks at 11.2 ms/frame with zero-shot generalization to low-light tasks.
AI.motivation: Single-shot exposure correction must handle under-exposure, over-exposure, and mixed spatial cases simultaneously. Existing methods lack formal guarantees on monotonicity and optimality, motivating a framework with provable structural properties (order preservation) and optimal transport-based global tone mapping.
AI.method: The framework decomposes correction into (1) a global monotone tone curve parameterized as the normalized cumulative integral of a strictly positive density, guaranteeing strict monotonicity by construction; (2) a differentiable sorted-sample Wasserstein-2 objective for training toward the OT optimum; and (3) a bounded local residual decoder with dual-branch convex fusion for spatially varying effects, with a proven sufficient condition for local order preservation.
AI.result: AutoLumNet achieves state-of-the-art PSNR and SSIM on five benchmarks (MSEC, SICE, LCDP, LOL-v1, LOL-v2-real) for both under- and over-exposure regimes, runs at 11.2 ms per frame, and generalizes zero-shot to low-light benchmarks without retraining.
AI.conclusion: AutoLumNet is the first exposure-correction method to simultaneously provide structural monotonicity, optimal-transport optimality, and bounded local adaptivity in a single trainable architecture, offering both theoretical guarantees and empirical SOTA performance.

title: A 360-Degree Vision Dataset for Learning Yaw Control on GPS-Denied Micro-UAVs in Disaster-Response-Relevant Environments
comment: Accepted at the 2026 IEEE/ASME International Conference on Advanced Intelligent Mechatronics (AIM), Genoa, Italy, July 6-10, 2026
summary: This paper presents a novel data-driven approach to camera-based autonomy for micro-drones in GPS-denied, radio-challenging indoor environments. The target application is disaster and emergency response, where micro-UAVs can provide rapid situational awareness in hazardous settings such as firefighting and chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) incidents while reducing risk for human responders. When the communication link is lost, the micro-drone uses a learned yaw controller to autonomously navigate toward open space, preserving onboard sensor data that would otherwise be lost with the vehicle. A custom micro-drone equipped with a 360-degree camera was used to record diverse industrial, underground, and training scenarios representative of communication-denied field operations. We introduce a preprocessing pipeline that converts equirectangular 360-degree footage into planar front views and dynamically generates image-label pairs for AI training. We then train and compare multiple convolutional neural network variants that predict a continuous yaw command from a single monocular view. Evaluation on a held-out test set confirms the feasibility of the learned yaw-prediction approach. A semi-autonomous real-world test further demonstrates the practicality of the method while revealing key failure modes, particularly reflections and glare.

AI.tldr: A data-driven approach for micro-drone autonomy in GPS-denied indoor environments, using a learned yaw controller with 360-degree camera imagery to navigate toward open space when communication is lost, validated through training and real-world semi-autonomous tests.
AI.motivation: To enable micro-UAVs to provide situational awareness in disaster and emergency response scenarios (firefighting, CBRN incidents) even when communication links fail, preserving onboard sensor data that would otherwise be lost.
AI.method: A custom micro-drone with a 360-degree camera records diverse indoor scenarios. A preprocessing pipeline converts equirectangular 360-degree footage into planar front views and dynamically generates image-label pairs. Multiple convolutional neural network variants are trained to predict continuous yaw commands from single monocular views.
AI.result: Evaluation on a held-out test set confirms feasibility of the learned yaw-prediction approach. A semi-autonomous real-world test demonstrates practicality but reveals key failure modes, particularly reflections and glare.
AI.conclusion: The learned yaw-prediction approach is feasible for autonomous navigation in communication-denied environments, though reflections and glare remain significant challenges to address in future work.

title: DIFFCZSL: Compositional Zero-Shot Learning Regularized by Diffusion Representations
summary: Compositional Zero-Shot Learning (CZSL) aims to recognize unseen attribute-object compositions by leveraging knowledge of primitive concepts learned from seen compositions. Although recent works achieve impressive performance in CZSL by leveraging large vision-language models, they primarily rely on discriminative representations that may not explicitly preserve the structured relationships between primitive concepts and their compositions. Motivated by the recent success of diffusion-based classifiers and their competitive performance relative to discriminative models, we investigate whether intermediate diffusion representations can provide complementary cues for CZSL. To this end, we propose DIFFCZSL, a diffusion-augmented framework that injects generative priors from pre-trained diffusion models into CLIP-based CZSL pipelines. We extract intermediate diffusion representations and project them into the CLIP embedding space to provide auxiliary supervision on both image and text modalities. Through contrastive alignment between CLIP embeddings and diffusion features during training, our method encourages the embedding geometry toward richer composition-aware semantics, while introducing no additional cost at inference time. Extensive experiments on three public CZSL benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over strong CLIP-based baselines under both closed-world and open-world settings. Our results highlight the complementary strengths of generative diffusion representations and discriminative vision-language models for compositional generalization.

AI.tldr: DIFFCZSL is a diffusion-augmented framework that injects generative priors from pre-trained diffusion models into CLIP-based Compositional Zero-Shot Learning (CZSL) pipelines, achieving consistent improvements on three benchmarks in both closed-world and open-world settings with no additional inference cost.
AI.motivation: Existing CZSL methods leveraging large vision-language models rely on discriminative representations that may not explicitly preserve structured relationships between primitive concepts and their compositions. The authors investigate whether complementary generative representations from diffusion models can address this limitation.
AI.method: DIFFCZSL extracts intermediate diffusion representations and projects them into the CLIP embedding space to provide auxiliary supervision on both image and text modalities, using contrastive alignment between CLIP embeddings and diffusion features during training.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on three public CZSL benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over strong CLIP-based baselines under both closed-world and open-world settings.
AI.conclusion: Generative diffusion representations and discriminative vision-language models offer complementary strengths for compositional generalization, and diffusion-based priors can be effectively injected into CLIP-based pipelines at no additional inference cost.

title: Unified and Efficient Point-Line Local Features
summary: Multi-view computer vision pipelines typically rely on accurate sparse keypoints and robust descriptors. While incorporating line features has shown clear benefits for matching and pose estimation, existing point-line approaches remain inefficient: they detect points and lines separately, use increasingly heavy networks, and depend on CPU-bound heuristics that hinder real-time performance. We introduce a Unified Efficient Points and Lines (UPAL) feature extractor that jointly extracts keypoints, line segments, and feature descriptors within a single lightweight architecture. A shared backbone provides common representations that feed different branches for point and line features. Line segments are recovered through an accelerated post-processing stage, an enhanced and highly efficient variant of the LSD algorithm. UPAL matches or exceeds state-ofthe-art performance in both point and line applications while significantly reducing computational cost, achieving, for instance, a 4x speedup and 10x smaller memory footprint over the ALIKED + DeepLSD pipeline. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/francois141/upal.

AI.tldr: UPAL is a unified lightweight architecture that jointly extracts keypoints, line segments, and descriptors from a shared backbone, with an accelerated LSD-based post-processing stage for line recovery. It matches or exceeds state-of-the-art point-line pipelines while achieving 4x speedup and 10x smaller memory footprint over ALIKED + DeepLSD.
AI.motivation: Existing point-line feature extraction pipelines are inefficient because they detect points and lines separately using heavy networks and CPU-bound heuristics, hindering real-time performance in multi-view computer vision tasks.
AI.method: UPAL uses a shared backbone to provide common representations feeding separate branches for point and line features. Line segments are recovered via an enhanced, highly efficient variant of the LSD algorithm in an accelerated post-processing stage.
AI.result: UPAL matches or exceeds state-of-the-art performance in point and line applications while significantly reducing computational cost, achieving 4x speedup and 10x smaller memory footprint compared to ALIKED + DeepLSD.
AI.conclusion: UPAL demonstrates that unified lightweight point-line feature extraction is feasible and efficient, enabling real-time multi-view pipelines without sacrificing accuracy.

title: AvatarDynamizer: From Static to Dynamic Human Avatars via Generative Dynamic Textures
summary: For full-body avatars, modeling surface dynamics is crucial for overcoming the uncanny valley and achieving perceptual realism. Person-agnostic methods recover static 3D avatars from monocular images, videos, or text prompts, but their skeleton-driven animations lack realistic surface dynamics such as clothing wrinkles. In contrast, person-specific methods achieve high-quality rendering and realistic dynamics, but require expensive multi-view captures for each individual. Recent generalizable dynamic avatar methods struggle to embed surface dynamics, leading to either limited multi-view consistency or dynamic expressiveness. To this end, we propose AvatarDynamizer, a generative method that transforms an off-the-shelf static 3D avatar into a controllable, realistic, and multi-view-consistent 4D avatar. We introduce a novel texture-space surface-dynamics embedding and formulate avatar dynamics modeling as conditional texture generation. Our encoder--decoder representation embeds pose-dependent dynamics into dynamic texture maps, enabling compatibility with pre-trained video diffusion models while decoding them into 3D Gaussians for multi-view consistent rendering. Since existing datasets are limited in scale, sequence length, or motion diversity, we collect a large-scale multi-view dataset with long sequences covering diverse skeletal motions and surface dynamics. Experiments show that our method effectively animates static avatars with faithful surface dynamics and outperforms competing generalizable methods in visual fidelity, especially under limited dynamic training data.

AI.tldr: AvatarDynamizer is a generative method that transforms off-the-shelf static 3D avatars into controllable, realistic, and multi-view-consistent 4D avatars by embedding pose-dependent surface dynamics into dynamic texture maps, enabling compatibility with pre-trained video diffusion models and decoding into 3D Gaussians for multi-view consistent rendering.
AI.motivation: Full-body avatars require realistic surface dynamics (e.g., clothing wrinkles) to overcome the uncanny valley. Person-agnostic methods lack realistic dynamics, person-specific methods require expensive multi-view captures, and existing generalizable dynamic avatar methods struggle to embed surface dynamics effectively.
AI.method: The paper introduces a texture-space surface-dynamics embedding that formulates avatar dynamics modeling as conditional texture generation. An encoder-decoder representation embeds pose-dependent dynamics into dynamic texture maps, works with pre-trained video diffusion models, and decodes them into 3D Gaussians for multi-view-consistent rendering. A large-scale multi-view dataset with long sequences covering diverse skeletal motions and surface dynamics is also collected.
AI.result: Experiments show the method effectively animates static avatars with faithful surface dynamics and outperforms competing generalizable methods in visual fidelity, especially under limited dynamic training data.
AI.conclusion: AvatarDynamizer successfully bridges the gap between person-agnostic and person-specific avatar methods by providing a generalizable yet dynamic approach, enabled by a novel texture-space dynamics embedding and a large-scale multi-view dataset.

title: Flow Matching Meets 3D Curvilinear Structure Segmentation in Medical Imaging
comment: International Workshop on Machine Learning in Medical Imaging (MLMI 2026) @ MICCAI
summary: Segmentation of curvilinear anatomical structures in 3D medical images remains challenging due to complex topology, severe class imbalance, weak contrast, and large variations in structure morphology. While deep learning approaches for 3D curvilinear segmentation have been proposed, they are often tailored to specific anatomies or modalities, limiting generalization across clinical settings and leaving room for improvement. Recent generative models have shown the benefits of iterative prediction for structured segmentation tasks, yet diffusion-based methods suffer from computationally expensive sampling, hindering their use on high-resolution 3D volumes. We present 3D-CurvSegFlow, a flow matching-based model for 3D curvilinear structure segmentation. The model learns a continuous transformation from a simple source distribution to the target vascular representation, enabling progressive refinement of complex curvilinear geometries with efficient inference. We evaluate our method on Three public challenging datasets covering distinct anatomies and modalities: portal vein, cerebral vessel, and coronary arteries. Using a common architecture and training strategy across all tasks, our method outperforms general-purpose and vessel-specific approaches, with strong preservation of thin branches and vascular continuity. This work not only advances the state-of-the-art in 3D curvilinear segmentation but also opens new avenues for efficient, generalizable, and clinically applicable methods in medical image analysis.

AI.tldr: 3D-CurvSegFlow is a flow matching-based deep learning model for segmenting curvilinear anatomical structures (vessels) in 3D medical images, which outperforms general-purpose and vessel-specific methods across three public datasets covering different anatomies and modalities, while offering more efficient inference than diffusion-based approaches.
AI.motivation: 3D curvilinear structure segmentation (e.g., vessels) is challenging due to complex topology, class imbalance, weak contrast, and morphological variation. Existing deep learning methods are often anatomy- or modality-specific, limiting generalization, while diffusion-based generative approaches suffer from computationally expensive sampling on high-resolution 3D volumes.
AI.method: The paper proposes 3D-CurvSegFlow, a flow matching-based model that learns a continuous transformation from a simple source distribution to the target vascular representation, enabling progressive refinement of complex curvilinear geometries with efficient inference compared to diffusion-based alternatives.
AI.result: Evaluated on three public challenging datasets (portal vein, cerebral vessel, coronary arteries), the method outperforms both general-purpose and vessel-specific segmentation approaches under a common architecture and training strategy, with strong preservation of thin branches and vascular continuity.
AI.conclusion: This work advances the state-of-the-art in 3D curvilinear segmentation and demonstrates potential for efficient, generalizable, and clinically applicable methods in medical image analysis.

title: Open-Vocabulary 3D Object Detection with Co-Distillation Discovery and Dual Guidance Robust Training
summary: Recently, open-vocabulary 3D object detection (3D-OVD) has gained increasing attention for its ability to detect unseen objects in 3D scenes. Existing approaches typically adopt a two-stage pipeline that first discovers novel objects using foundation models and then trains a 3D-OVD model based on these discovered objects. Although effective, this pipeline often suffers from inaccurate localization and mismatched classification during the discovery stage, which subsequently limits the performance of the model training stage. To address these limitations, we advocate for improving both the reliability of novel object discovery and the robustness of model training, and propose an innovative framework. Specifically, for reliable discovery, our co-distillation strategy distills high-quality novel objects by applying Hungarian matching over a comprehensive score that incorporates geometric consistency, structural objectness, and semantic certainty. To enhance robust model training, we further propose a dual-guidance learning scheme, incorporating a scene-awareness-guided uncertainty regularization for the regression head and an LLM-guided hierarchical alignment for the classification head, effectively mitigating the negative effects of imprecise 3D bounding boxes and semantic ambiguity. Extensive experiments on SUN RGB-D and ScanNetV2 demonstrate that our method achieves significant performance gains over state-of-the-art approaches. Code is available at https://github.com/shangboyuan/Co-3DGT

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Co-3DGT, a framework for open-vocabulary 3D object detection that improves both novel object discovery reliability and model training robustness. It uses co-distillation with Hungarian matching based on a comprehensive scoring function for discovery, and a dual-guidance learning scheme (scene-awareness-guided uncertainty regularization for regression, LLM-guided hierarchical alignment for classification) for training. Experiments on SUN RGB-D and ScanNetV2 show significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods.
AI.motivation: Existing two-stage open-vocabulary 3D object detection pipelines suffer from inaccurate localization and mismatched classification during the discovery stage, which limits downstream model training performance. The authors aim to address both the reliability of novel object discovery and the robustness of model training.
AI.method: The framework has two key components: (1) A co-distillation strategy that distills high-quality novel objects by applying Hungarian matching over a comprehensive score combining geometric consistency, structural objectness, and semantic certainty for reliable discovery. (2) A dual-guidance learning scheme featuring scene-awareness-guided uncertainty regularization for the regression head and LLM-guided hierarchical alignment for the classification head to mitigate imprecise 3D bounding boxes and semantic ambiguity during training.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on SUN RGB-D and ScanNetV2 benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant performance gains over state-of-the-art open-vocabulary 3D object detection approaches.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively addresses the limitations of existing two-stage open-vocabulary 3D object detection pipelines by jointly improving novel object discovery quality and training robustness, yielding state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks.

title: STEP: Score-Based Temporal Energy for Human Pose Video Anomaly Detection
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026. Project page: https://jakubmicorek.github.io/STEP-demo | Code: https://github.com/jakubmicorek/STEP
summary: Skeleton-based Video Anomaly Detection (VAD) offers a robust, privacy-preserving solution for identifying abnormal behaviors. To model the distribution of normal static and moving poses, recent methods train Energy-Based Models (EBMs) via Denoising Score Matching (DSM). However, directly injecting noise, required for training, into raw joint coordinates creates physically impossible poses, and this structural collapse severely worsens as the temporal window expands. To address this, we introduce STEP, a simple framework that utilizes Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to project pose sequences into a compact, whitened PC-space. Learning the data density within this well-behaved PC-space ensures that the injected noise translates into physically plausible variations, which allows the model to process longer video sequences without the performance collapse of raw coordinate baselines. Additionally, to mitigate inherent pose estimation inaccuracies arising from occlusions or motion blur, we integrate a sequence-level weighting mechanism based on the estimator's confidence scores. Operating at real-time computational efficiency, our simple and lightweight framework outperforms the previous skeleton-based state-of-the-art by 12.2% (90.1% AUROC) on the challenging UBnormal dataset and achieves highly competitive results by improving on the ShanghaiTech benchmark.

AI.tldr: STEP is a lightweight skeleton-based video anomaly detection framework that projects pose sequences into a whitened PC-space via PCA before training Energy-Based Models with Denoising Score Matching, preventing structural collapse from noise injection and enabling longer temporal windows. It achieves 90.1% AUROC on UBnormal (12.2% improvement over prior SOTA) with real-time efficiency.
AI.motivation: Existing EBM-based skeleton VAD methods using Denoising Score Matching suffer from structural collapse when noise is injected into raw joint coordinates, creating physically impossible poses—a problem that worsens with longer temporal windows and limits model performance.
AI.method: STEP uses Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to project pose sequences into a compact, whitened PC-space where noise injection produces physically plausible variations, allowing longer video sequence processing. It also incorporates a sequence-level weighting mechanism based on pose estimator confidence scores to handle inaccuracies from occlusions or motion blur.
AI.result: STEP outperforms prior skeleton-based state-of-the-art by 12.2% (90.1% AUROC) on the UBnormal dataset and achieves highly competitive results on ShanghaiTech, all while operating at real-time computational efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Projecting pose sequences into PCA-whitened space resolves the structural collapse problem in score-based EBM training for skeleton VAD, enabling longer temporal processing and superior detection performance with a simple, lightweight, and real-time framework.

title: Point-Based 3D Reconstruction from Sparse Views under Known Illumination
summary:
Sparse view 3D reconstruction is commonly addressed with neural implicit surfaces or dense point-based representations such as Gaussian splatting. Surface-aware splatting methods improve extracted geometry through oriented primitives and regularization, while RadiosityGS incorporates differentiable light transport through a radiosity inspired finite-element surfel formulation. We propose a differentiable point rendering method based on opacity-bearing beta surfels. An opacity explicit adjoint light transport formulation provides gradients for surfel geometry and appearance parameters, allowing physically based light transport to constrain reconstruction.
  Across five synthetic objects reconstructed from ten posed views, our method achieves the lowest mean symmetric Chamfer distance among the evaluated baselines and reduces mean Chamfer distance by 28.5% relative to the strongest point-based baseline while using only 267 surfels on average, approximately ~161 fewer primitives. Directional Chamfer results further show improved accuracy and competitive completion relative to related point-based methods. These results show that, in the controlled direct illumination setting, compact beta surfels combined with transport-based optimization can recover surfaces without relying on the tens to hundreds of thousands of primitives used by the evaluated baselines.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a differentiable point-based 3D reconstruction method using opacity-bearing beta surfels with an explicit adjoint light transport formulation, achieving the lowest Chamfer distance among baselines using only ~267 surfels on average.
AI.motivation: Sparse view 3D reconstruction faces challenges: neural implicit surfaces and dense point-based methods like Gaussian splatting require many primitives or lack physical accuracy. The authors aim to recover compact, accurate surfaces by incorporating physically based light transport into optimization.
AI.method: The method uses opacity-bearing beta surfels for differentiable point rendering. An opacity explicit adjoint light transport formulation provides gradients for surfel geometry and appearance, enabling physically based light transport to constrain the reconstruction.
AI.result: Across five synthetic objects from ten posed views, the method achieves the lowest mean symmetric Chamfer distance among evaluated baselines, reducing mean Chamfer distance by 28.5% relative to the strongest point-based baseline while using only 267 surfels on average (~161 fewer primitives). Directional Chamfer results show improved accuracy and competitive completion.
AI.conclusion: In the controlled direct illumination setting, compact beta surfels combined with transport-based optimization can recover accurate surfaces without relying on the tens to hundreds of thousands of primitives used by evaluated baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of physically based constraints in compact point-based reconstruction.

title: From Street View Imagery to Street Quality Indicators: Vision Language Inference for the Suburban 15-minute City
summary: Streetscape quality has become a central concern in contemporary urban planning, particularly within the framework of the pedestrian-friendly 15-minute city, where walkability and public-space quality are increasingly recognized as key determinants of urban performance. However, assessing streetscape qualities across large suburban and peri-urban territories remains challenging due to the time and resource demands of conventional field surveys. This paper presents a planning-oriented assessment of streetscape qualities in the north-eastern periphery of Nice (France) using the latest release of SAGAI (Streetscape Analysis with Generative AI), an open-source workflow that leverages vision-language models (VLMs) for large-scale streetscape analysis from Google Street View imagery. The new release addresses limitations of the original framework through improved image acquisition, geographically consistent view generation, support for multiple VLM architectures, consensus-based inference, and an integrated analytical environment. The workflow is applied to several thousand street-level observations to evaluate qualities relevant to pedestrian-friendly urban environments: sidewalk presence, pedestrian entrance density, and vegetation. The resulting maps reveal that the desired streetscape qualities characterize only a fraction of today's suburban streetscapes, mainly in compact developments and traditional suburban faubourgs, while they are particularly lacking on residential hills. The analysis demonstrates the potential of contemporary VLMs to support urban diagnostics in extensive suburban territories where fieldwork would be prohibitively time-consuming. Beyond the case study, the paper illustrates how recent advances in vision-language models can contribute to evidence-based planning by enabling scalable, flexible, and interpretable assessments of urban public-space quality.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an updated SAGAI workflow using vision-language models (VLMs) to assess streetscape quality across large suburban areas, applied to Nice's north-eastern periphery, revealing that pedestrian-friendly qualities are only found in compact developments and traditional faubourgs while largely absent in residential hills.
AI.motivation: Assessing streetscape quality across large suburban and peri-urban territories is challenging due to the time and resource demands of conventional field surveys, yet such assessment is central to pedestrian-friendly urban planning like the 15-minute city framework.
AI.method: The authors use the latest release of SAGAI, an open-source workflow leveraging vision-language models for large-scale streetscape analysis from Google Street View imagery, with improvements including better image acquisition, geographically consistent view generation, support for multiple VLM architectures, consensus-based inference, and an integrated analytical environment. The workflow evaluates sidewalk presence, pedestrian entrance density, and vegetation across thousands of street-level observations.
AI.result: Maps show that desired streetscape qualities characterize only a fraction of today's suburban streetscapes, found mainly in compact developments and traditional suburban faubourgs, while being particularly lacking on residential hills. The analysis demonstrates the potential of contemporary VLMs to support urban diagnostics in extensive suburban territories where fieldwork would be prohibitively time-consuming.
AI.conclusion: Recent advances in vision-language models can contribute to evidence-based planning by enabling scalable, flexible, and interpretable assessments of urban public-space quality beyond traditional fieldwork constraints.

title: Gravity-aware partially calibrated absolute pose estimation from affine- or rotation-covariant features
summary: Inertial measurement units (IMUs) are now standard in most consumer devices, such as smartphones, drones, and extended reality (XR) headsets. By fusing visual and inertial data, localization systems gain significantly in speed and robustness compared to vision-only or IMU-only approaches. However, traditional pose estimation methods fail to utilize the local geometric information embedded in feature descriptors like SIFT. Recent work has proved the advantages of leveraging this information for relative and absolute pose estimation, but its application to partially calibrated absolute pose estimation remains unexplored. In this paper, we derive novel constraints for joint estimation of absolute pose and focal length, making use of a gravity vector obtained from IMU data and the feature-induced local geometry, which we use to construct two efficient solvers: UP1PfAC, that operates given a single affine correspondence and UP2PfORI, which requires two orientation-covariant features. Unlike traditional, semi-calibrated absolute pose methods requiring four point correspondences, our solvers benefit from fewer samples and lower computational cost, simplifying robust estimation in modern RANSAC-like frameworks. We evaluate the proposed solvers against the state-of-the-art on large-scale public datasets and demonstrate that our method achieves fast and accurate localization and focal length estimation.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces two new solvers (UP1PfAC and UP2PfORI) for jointly estimating absolute camera pose and focal length by leveraging IMU-provided gravity vectors and local geometric information from feature descriptors, requiring only one affine correspondence or two orientation-covariant features respectively—significantly fewer than the four point correspondences needed by traditional semi-calibrated methods.
AI.motivation: While prior work has shown the benefits of using local geometric information from feature descriptors (e.g., SIFT) for relative and absolute pose estimation, this has not yet been applied to partially calibrated absolute pose estimation (where focal length must also be estimated). The authors aim to fill this gap and reduce the sample requirements of traditional semi-calibrated pose methods.
AI.method: The authors derive novel constraints that jointly estimate absolute pose and focal length by combining a gravity vector from IMU data with feature-induced local geometry. Based on these constraints, they construct two efficient solvers: UP1PfAC (using a single affine correspondence) and UP2PfORI (requiring two orientation-covariant features).
AI.result: Evaluation on large-scale public datasets shows that the proposed solvers achieve fast and accurate localization and focal length estimation compared to state-of-the-art methods, while requiring fewer samples and lower computational cost for robust estimation in RANSAC-like frameworks.
AI.conclusion: The paper successfully demonstrates that local geometric information from feature descriptors can be effectively exploited for partially calibrated absolute pose estimation, yielding faster and more accurate localization with IMU- aided visual-inertial systems.

title: V-REX: Efficient Specialist VLM Training for Veterinary X-Rays
summary: While generalist VLMs are expensive to train, creating domain experts is widely assumed to require fine-tuning increasingly large foundation models. We show that, in veterinary radiology, this assumption is misguided. By rethinking the entire VLM pipeline - from text tokenisation and pre-training to grounding and inference - we demonstrate that careful engineering can yield models that outperform much larger foundation models from scratch, without relying on any other data. Our approach introduces new strategies for generative pre-training and grounding that improve training efficiency, increasing data utilisation and downstream performance. Using only a fraction of the parameters, data, and compute of contemporary generalist models, we develop the first VLM capable of generating diagnostic reports for veterinary radiographs, surpassing open foundation models on this task by significant margin.

AI.tldr: This paper challenges the assumption that domain experts require fine-tuning increasingly large foundation models. By rethinking the entire VLM pipeline (tokenisation, pre-training, grounding, inference), the authors build a veterinary radiology VLM from scratch that outperforms much larger foundation models with a fraction of parameters, data, and compute—achieving state-of-the-art diagnostic report generation for veterinary radiographs.
AI.motivation: Generalist VLMs are expensive to train, and the prevailing assumption is that domain experts must be built by fine-tuning ever-larger foundation models. The authors aim to challenge this assumption by demonstrating that careful engineering of the full pipeline can yield superior domain experts from scratch, using far fewer resources.
AI.method: The authors rethink the entire VLM pipeline, introducing new strategies for generative pre-training and grounding that improve training efficiency, data utilisation, and downstream performance. The approach does not rely on any external data beyond the target domain.
AI.result: The resulting model is the first VLM capable of generating diagnostic reports for veterinary radiographs, surpassing open foundation models on this task by a significant margin while using only a fraction of the parameters, data, and compute of generalist counterparts.
AI.conclusion: Careful engineering across the full VLM pipeline can outperform large foundation models in narrow domains without expensive fine-tuning of huge backbones, suggesting that domain-specific models can be built efficiently from scratch.

title: HandMvNet: Real-Time 3D Hand Pose Estimation Using Multi-View Cross-Attention Fusion
summary: In this work, we present HandMvNet, one of the first real-time method designed to estimate 3D hand motion and shape from multi-view camera images. Unlike previous monocular approaches, which suffer from scale-depth ambiguities, our method ensures consistent and accurate absolute hand poses and shapes. This is achieved through a multi-view attention-fusion mechanism that effectively integrates features from multiple viewpoints. In contrast to previous multi-view methods, our approach eliminates the need for camera parameters as input to learn 3D geometry. HandMvNet also achieves a substantial reduction in inference time while delivering competitive results compared to the state-of-the-art methods, making it suitable for real-time applications. Evaluated on publicly available datasets, HandMvNet qualitatively and quantitatively outperforms previous methods under identical settings. Code is available at github.com/pyxploiter/handmvnet.

AI.tldr: HandMvNet is a real-time multi-view 3D hand pose and shape estimation method that uses a multi-view attention-fusion mechanism to integrate features from multiple camera angles. It eliminates the need for camera parameters as input, avoids scale-depth ambiguities common in monocular approaches, and achieves competitive accuracy with substantially reduced inference time compared to state-of-the-art methods.
AI.motivation: Monocular 3D hand estimation suffers from scale-depth ambiguities, and existing multi-view methods are computationally expensive and often require camera parameters as input. The authors aim to develop a real-time multi-view approach that produces accurate, consistent absolute hand poses and shapes.
AI.method: HandMvNet employs a multi-view attention-fusion mechanism to effectively integrate features from multiple camera viewpoints without requiring camera parameters as input for learning 3D geometry. This design enables consistent and accurate absolute hand pose and shape estimation in real-time.
AI.result: HandMvNet achieves competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods while substantially reducing inference time, making it suitable for real-time applications. It qualitatively and quantitatively outperforms previous methods under identical settings on publicly available datasets.
AI.conclusion: HandMvNet demonstrates that real-time multi-view hand pose and shape estimation is achievable without camera parameters, overcoming the limitations of both monocular and previous multi-view approaches while maintaining state-of-the-art competitiveness.

title: Structured Affinity for Unsupervised Visual Class-Incremental Memory in Deep Artificial Immune Networks
summary: Artificial immune networks (AINs) are naturally memory-forming systems, but conventional visual AINs often rely on flattened vector affinity that ignores spatial structure. This paper studies whether structured, gradient-free immune affinity can make Deep AINs viable as replay-free visual class-incremental representation-memory learners. Visual B-cells are formalized as structured templates, including shifted-template affinity, zero-normalized cross-correlation (ZNCC) filters, and feature-map binding profiles. A repertoire is treated both as memory and as a representation-inducing basis, while depth is obtained by passing binding-profile response maps to subsequent immune layers. The resulting Deep AIN exhibits adaptive latent coordinate reorganization: as new classes arrive, the binding-profile space evolves while retaining recoverable structure for earlier classes. Experiments on sklearn digits, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and KMNIST show that preserving response maps is critical. Scalar binding-profile variants underperform, whereas feature-map Deep AINs learn class-discriminative visual memory without replay, label-driven immune updates, or backpropagation through the immune layers. On sklearn digits, downstream probes fitted on the learned binding profiles reach 0.939 final balanced accuracy with logistic regression and 0.902 with 1-nearest-neighbour after all ten classes are encountered, with initial-class retention of 0.978. Adaptive layer-wise scale calibration further improves the two-layer feature-map Deep AIN to 0.978 balanced accuracy. With the same calibration rule, Fashion-MNIST reaches 0.814 and KMNIST reaches 0.853. These probes are external validation tools, not components of the AIN. The results identify structured affinity, response-map preservation, adaptive latent reorganization, and layer-wise scale calibration as key mechanisms for replay-free visual immune memory.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether structured, gradient-free immune affinity can make Deep Artificial Immune Networks (AINs) viable as replay-free visual class-incremental memory learners. By formalizing visual B-cells as structured templates (shifted-template affinity, ZNCC filters, feature-map binding profiles) and stacking immune layers, the Deep AIN achieves adaptive latent reorganization that preserves earlier-class structure. Experiments on sklearn digits (0.978 balanced accuracy with calibration), Fashion-MNIST (0.814), and KMNIST (0.853) show feature-map Deep AINs learn class-discriminative visual memory without replay, label-driven updates, or backpropagation.
AI.motivation: Conventional visual AINs rely on flattened vector affinity that ignores spatial structure, yet AINs are naturally memory-forming systems. The paper asks whether structured affinity can make Deep AINs viable as replay-free class-incremental learners, addressing the gap between AINs' natural memory capabilities and their lack of spatial awareness.
AI.method: Visual B-cells are formalized as structured templates with shifted-template affinity, zero-normalized cross-correlation (ZNCC) filters, and feature-map binding profiles. The repertoire serves as both memory and representation-inducing basis. Depth comes from passing binding-profile response maps to subsequent immune layers. A two-layer architecture with adaptive layer-wise scale calibration is evaluated, with downstream probes (logistic regression, kNN) used only as external validation, not components of the AIN.
AI.result: On sklearn digits, probes reach 0.939 (logistic regression) and 0.902 (1-NN) final balanced accuracy after all ten classes, with initial-class retention of 0.978. Adaptive layer-wise scale calibration improves the two-layer feature-map Deep AIN to 0.978 balanced accuracy. Fashion-MNIST reaches 0.814 and KMNIST 0.853 with the same calibration. Scalar binding-profile variants underperform, confirming response-map preservation is critical.
AI.conclusion: Structured affinity, response-map preservation, adaptive latent reorganization, and layer-wise scale calibration are identified as key mechanisms for replay-free visual immune memory. Feature-map Deep AINs can learn class-discriminative visual memory without replay, label-driven immune updates, or backpropagation through immune layers.

title: BeyondMasks: Evaluating Causal and Physical Consistency in Video Object Removal
summary: Recent advances in generative video models have significantly improved visual realism in video object removal, yet evaluation protocols still focus on masked region fidelity, treating removal as local inpainting. In real scenes, object removal is a causal intervention: eliminating an object also requires removing its induced physical effects, such as shadows, reflections, illumination changes, translucency, and dynamic traces. Existing benchmarks lack aligned clean references or remain limited to simplified synthetic settings, preventing systematic evaluation of causal consistency. We introduce BeyondMasks, a paired benchmark for causally consistent video object removal, consisting of temporally aligned synthetic and real world video pairs with clean background references. The dataset spans diverse photometric, geometric, volumetric, and dynamic interactions, and supports both mask based and instruction driven editing. We further propose CORE, a structured vision language model based evaluation protocol that jointly measures object disappearance and after effect consistency, aligning more closely with human judgments than existing metrics. Benchmarking state of the art methods reveals systematic failures in removing secondary physical effects despite high masked region fidelity, exposing a gap between visual plausibility and causal correctness. BeyondMasks reframes video object removal as causal scene consistency rather than local reconstruction and provides a unified framework for its evaluation.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces BeyondMasks, a paired benchmark for causally consistent video object removal with clean background references, plus CORE, a vision-language-model-based evaluation protocol measuring object disappearance and after-effect consistency. Benchmarking shows SOTA methods fail to remove secondary physical effects despite high masked-region fidelity, reframing removal as causal scene consistency.
AI.motivation: Existing video object removal evaluation focuses only on masked region fidelity (local inpainting), ignoring that real object removal is a causal intervention requiring elimination of induced physical effects like shadows, reflections, illumination changes, translucency, and dynamic traces. Current benchmarks lack aligned clean references or remain in simplified synthetic settings, preventing systematic evaluation of causal consistency.
AI.method: The paper introduces BeyondMasks, a paired benchmark with temporally aligned synthetic and real-world video pairs and clean background references, spanning diverse photometric, geometric, volumetric, and dynamic interactions. It supports both mask-based and instruction-driven editing. The paper also proposes CORE, a structured vision-language-model-based evaluation protocol that jointly measures object disappearance and after-effect consistency.
AI.result: Benchmarking state-of-the-art methods reveals systematic failures in removing secondary physical effects despite high masked region fidelity, exposing a gap between visual plausibility and causal correctness. CORE aligns more closely with human judgments than existing metrics.
AI.conclusion: BeyondMasks reframes video object removal as causal scene consistency rather than local reconstruction, and provides a unified framework for its evaluation, highlighting the need for methods to address physical after-effects of removed objects.

title: ArmorOCR: Grounded Adversarial Visual Perception via Observation-Transferred Self-Distillation
summary: Large multimodal models (LMMs) have demonstrated strong OCR recognition capabilities, yet remain vulnerable to adversarial visual text that is readable to humans but challenging for models to localize and recognize. Existing OCR benchmarks mainly focus on natural or document-style text, while adversarial OCR evaluations remain limited in scale, task coverage, or region-aware evaluation. In this paper, we formulate adversarial OCR as a \textbf{grounded OCR perception} task and introduce \textbf{AdvSpot}, the first benchmark for grounded adversarial OCR evaluation. AdvSpot comprises 390 images with region-level annotations, spanning 5 primary categories and 13 fine-grained adversarial OCR types. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{ArmorOCR}, a two-stage training framework for robust adversarial OCR perception. ArmorOCR first acquires missing adversarial OCR perception from privileged transformed observations through On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), and then refines grounded OCR perception through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with task-conditioned rewards for localization, recognition, full spotting, and visual question answering (VQA). Experiments on our AdvSpot, other adversarial OCR benchmarks, and general OCR benchmarks demonstrate that ArmorOCR consistently improves adversarial OCR perception while preserving competitive general OCR capability.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces AdvSpot, the first benchmark for grounded adversarial OCR evaluation with 390 region-level annotated images spanning 5 categories and 13 adversarial OCR types, and proposes ArmorOCR, a two-stage training framework combining On-Policy Self-Distillation and Group Relative Policy Optimization to improve adversarial OCR perception while preserving general OCR capability.
