AI.motivation: Large multimodal models are vulnerable to adversarial visual text that is readable to humans but difficult for models to perceive. Existing OCR benchmarks focus on natural or document text, while adversarial OCR evaluations are limited in scale, task coverage, or region-aware evaluation.
AI.method: ArmorOCR uses a two-stage training framework: (1) On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) to acquire missing adversarial OCR perception from privileged transformed observations, and (2) Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with task-conditioned rewards for localization, recognition, full spotting, and VQA.
AI.result: Experiments on AdvSpot, other adversarial OCR benchmarks, and general OCR benchmarks show that ArmorOCR consistently improves adversarial OCR perception while maintaining competitive general OCR capability.
AI.conclusion: The proposed benchmark and training framework effectively address grounded adversarial OCR perception, advancing robustness of LMMs against adversarial visual text without sacrificing general OCR performance.

title: ID-VTG: Image-Disambiguated Video Temporal Grounding
summary: Video Temporal Grounding (VTG) faces significant challenges when natural language queries must distinguish between multiple events involving visually similar entities, particularly when relying on fine-grained visual attributes that are difficult to describe accurately in words alone. To address this, we introduce Image-Disambiguated Video Temporal Grounding (ID-VTG), a task that leverages multimodal queries combining a reference image and a text description to precisely localize segments where a specific instance performs a described action. To facilitate research, we construct two benchmarks: IDVTG-Gym, focusing on fine-grained, compositionally ordered gymnastics actions with athletes in similar uniforms; and IDVTG-InternVid, an open-world dataset featuring diverse entities (e.g., humans, animals, fictional characters) and significant temporal distractors. Methodologically, we propose the Visually-Guided Disambiguation Aggregation (VGD-Agg) framework based on a dual-branch fast-slow architecture. The fast branch efficiently generates preliminary event proposals, while the slow branch performs fine-grained frame-level matching between video frames and the reference image. We enhance discriminability via two learnable tokens: a Compare Token, which represents hard negatives to probe for the presence of the target instance (as referred to by the query image), and a Depress Value, which represents text-irrelevant events. Proposals that the Compare Token identifies as lacking the target instance are pushed toward the Depress Value, thus easing disambiguation via the text query. Extensive experiments validate our approach, which achieves state-of-the-art results on the proposed benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/oceanflowlab/ID-VTG.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Image-Disambiguated Video Temporal Grounding (ID-VTG), a new task that uses multimodal queries (reference image + text) to localize video segments where a specific instance performs a described action, addressing challenges when events with visually similar entities are hard to distinguish via text alone. The authors construct two benchmarks (IDVTG-Gym and IDVTG-InternVid) and propose the VGD-Agg framework based on a dual-branch fast-slow architecture with Compare Token and Depress Value mechanisms, achieving state-of-the-art results.
AI.motivation: Video Temporal Grounding struggles when queries must distinguish between multiple events with visually similar entities, especially when fine-grained visual attributes are hard to describe accurately in text. A single-modality text query is insufficient for precise disambiguation in such cases.
AI.method: The paper proposes: (1) a new task formulation ID-VTG using multimodal queries (image + text); (2) two benchmarks, IDVTG-Gym (fine-grained gymnastics) and IDVTG-InternVid (open-world); and (3) the VGD-Agg framework with a dual-branch fast-slow architecture, where the fast branch generates preliminary proposals and the slow branch performs fine-grained frame-level matching against the reference image. Two learnable tokens enhance discriminability: a Compare Token (probes for presence of target instance as hard negatives) and a Depress Value (represents text-irrelevant events), pushing non-matching proposals away to ease disambiguation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments validate the proposed approach, which achieves state-of-the-art results on both proposed benchmarks (IDVTG-Gym and IDVTG-InternVid).
AI.conclusion: The ID-VTG task and VGD-Agg framework effectively address the challenge of distinguishing visually similar instances in video temporal grounding by leveraging image-disambiguated multimodal queries, with code made publicly available for further research.

title: Feature Evolution and Migration during Vision Transformer Training
summary: We present a novel view on feature evolution in Vision Transformers (ViTs) by visualizing the training process over two dimensions -- network depth (layer) and training time (epochs). We employ Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to extract candidate sparse features from CLS-token representations and compare their activation profiles across epoch--layer pairs. This allows us to study feature-level dynamics that are not directly visible from representation-level similarity measures. Furthermore, we demonstrate how this framework of feature evolution allows us to describe feature migration, the change in the layer where a feature is most detectable during training. Our experiments show that migration is concentrated early in training, occurs more often toward earlier layers than toward deeper layers, and declines as feature organization stabilizes. We further find that deeper layers stabilize earlier and more strongly than shallow layers. The results show that our approach can be employed as a tool for understanding how ViTs learn and evolve.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a framework for visualizing feature evolution in Vision Transformers (ViTs) across two dimensions—network depth (layer) and training time (epochs)—using Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to extract sparse features from CLS-token representations. The authors study "feature migration" (changes in which layer a feature is most detectable) and find migration is concentrated early in training, tends toward earlier layers, and declines as organization stabilizes, with deeper layers stabilizing earlier than shallow layers.
AI.motivation: Existing representation-level similarity measures in ViTs do not reveal fine-grained feature-level dynamics during training. The authors aim to understand how individual features evolve across both network depth and training time, which is not directly observable with current approaches.
AI.method: The approach uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to extract candidate sparse features from CLS-token representations in ViTs. Activation profiles of these features are compared across epoch-layer pairs, enabling the study of feature-level dynamics. The framework is used to describe feature migration—the layer where a feature is most detectable changing over training.
AI.result: Experiments show that feature migration is concentrated early in training, occurs more frequently toward earlier layers than deeper layers, and declines as feature organization stabilizes. Additionally, deeper layers stabilize earlier and more strongly than shallow layers.
AI.conclusion: The proposed feature-evolution framework serves as an effective tool for understanding how ViTs learn and evolve, providing insights into feature-level dynamics that complement representation-level analyses.

title: DPC-Net: Dual-Prior Collaborative Network for All-in-One Image Restoration
summary: All-in-One Image Restoration (AiOIR) aims to handle diverse degradations within a unified model. However, existing methods often overlook image semantics in degradation modeling and lack low-level visual priors during reconstruction, leading to structural distortions and semantic inconsistencies. To address these issues, we propose a novel Dual-Prior Collaborative Network (DPC-Net), which achieves high-quality restoration by jointly exploiting degradation-semantic coupled priors and low-level visual priors. Specifically, degraded images are fed into a Degradation-Aware Network (DAN) to extract degradation-semantic coupled features. To this end, a Vision-Language Model (VLM) supervises DAN by constraining its features distribution, introducing image semantics into the encoding of degradation patterns. A Degradation-Semantic Modulation Module (DSMM) further translates this guidance into degradation-semantic coupling and propagates coupled representations to the decoder. During decoding, knowledge bases provide low-level visual priors, and the Dual-Prior Collaborative Reconstruction Module (DPCR) integrates dual-prior information to guide degradation removal while preserving structure and semantics, producing high-fidelity restored images. Extensive experiments on multiple restoration benchmarks demonstrate that DPC-Net achieves superior performance against state-of-the-art AiOIR methods.

AI.tldr: DPC-Net is a novel All-in-One Image Restoration network that jointly exploits degradation-semantic coupled priors (guided by a Vision-Language Model) and low-level visual priors (from knowledge bases) via a Dual-Prior Collaborative Reconstruction Module, achieving state-of-the-art performance across multiple restoration benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing AiOIR methods overlook image semantics in degradation modeling and lack low-level visual priors during reconstruction, leading to structural distortions and semantic inconsistencies in restored images.
AI.method: DPC-Net consists of: (1) a Degradation-Aware Network (DAN) that extracts degradation-semantic coupled features, supervised by a Vision-Language Model (VLM) which constrains feature distributions to introduce semantics into degradation encoding; (2) a Degradation-Semantic Modulation Module (DSMM) that translates VLM guidance into degradation-semantic coupling and propagates coupled representations to the decoder; (3) knowledge bases providing low-level visual priors during decoding; and (4) a Dual-Prior Collaborative Reconstruction Module (DPCR) that integrates dual-prior information to guide degradation removal while preserving structure and semantics.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple restoration benchmarks demonstrate that DPC-Net achieves superior performance against state-of-the-art AiOIR methods.
AI.conclusion: By jointly exploiting degradation-semantic coupled priors and low-level visual priors, DPC-Net successfully addresses structural distortions and semantic inconsistencies in all-in-one image restoration, producing high-fidelity restored images.

title: PelviNeXt: A Modality-Agnostic Hybrid Network for Pelvic Imaging in Women's Health
summary: Women's health remains substantially under-resourced in medical imaging research, with pelvic pathologies such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and pelvic fracture both suffering from a scarcity of public, well-annotated benchmark data despite their clinical importance. We introduce PelviNeXt, a modality-agnostic hybrid architecture combining a dense convolutional feature extractor, hierarchical channel-spatial attention (H-CBAM), a multi-scale fusion module (MSFM), and talking-heads multi-head self-attention (TH-MHSA), applied without modification to both pelvic ultrasound and X-ray inputs. While benchmarking PelviNeXt on PCOSGen, the only gynaecologist-annotated public PCOS ultrasound dataset, we identified extensive exact and near-duplicate contamination within and across the dataset. We audit this contamination via perceptual hashing, publicly release a deduplicated version of the dataset, and establish the first integrity-audited evaluation protocol and baseline for PCOSGen under 5-fold cross-validation. On the only publicly available pelvic fracture X-ray dataset (PXR150), PelviNeXt exceeds previously reported state-of-the-art results across accuracy, recall, specificity, and AUROC. Ablation studies confirm that each architectural component contributes to performance on both tasks. Our results demonstrate that a single architecture, applied without task-specific modification, can serve as a reliable foundation for pelvic imaging across modalities in data-scarce, under-researched areas of women's health.

AI.tldr: PelviNeXt is a modality-agnostic hybrid architecture for pelvic imaging that combines a dense convolutional feature extractor, hierarchical channel-spatial attention (H-CBAM), multi-scale fusion (MSFM), and talking-heads multi-head self-attention (TH-MHSA). It is applied without modification to both pelvic ultrasound (PCOS) and X-ray (pelvic fracture) data. The paper also identifies and audits exact/near-duplicate contamination in PCOSGen via perceptual hashing, releases a deduplicated version, and establishes the first integrity-audited baseline. PelviNeXt exceeds prior state-of-the-art on PXR150 and ablation studies confirm each component's contribution.
AI.motivation: Women's health is under-resourced in medical imaging research, and pelvic pathologies like PCOS and pelvic fractures suffer from a scarcity of public, well-annotated benchmark datasets despite their clinical importance.
AI.method: PelviNeXt is built from four components: a dense convolutional feature extractor, hierarchical channel-spatial attention (H-CBAM), a multi-scale fusion module (MSFM), and talking-heads multi-head self-attention (TH-MHSA). It is applied unchanged to both ultrasound and X-ray inputs. The authors also used perceptual hashing to audit and deduplicate the PCOSGen dataset, and evaluated under 5-fold cross-validation.
AI.result: On PCOSGen, the paper identified extensive exact and near-duplicate contamination and released a deduplicated version with an integrity-audited evaluation protocol. On PXR150, PelviNeXt exceeded previous state-of-the-art in accuracy, recall, specificity, and AUROC. Ablation studies confirm each architectural component contributes on both tasks.
AI.conclusion: A single, task-agnostic architecture can serve as a reliable foundation for pelvic imaging across modalities in data-scarce, under-researched areas of women's health.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Workflow Analysis in Colorectal Surgery: A Multicentric, Cross-Procedural Development and Generalization Study
summary: Minimally invasive colorectal surgeries (MIS-CRS) are characterised by significant variability and inconsistent outcomes. ColoWorkflow, a tool for the video-based assessment (VBA) of MIS-CRS workflow, was recently validated. However, manual VBA is time-consuming, limiting implementation. This study presents AI-ColoWorkflow, a deep learning model for automated surgical workflow analysis across MIS-CRS. Operative videos of MIS-CRS were collected from 4 centres and a publicly available dataset. Phases and steps were manually annotated according to ColoWorkflow. A deep learning model combining a fine-tuned DINOv3 vision transformer for per-frame visual feature extraction with a hierarchical multi-stage temporal convolutional network was jointly optimized for phase and step recognition. The model trained on pooled multicentric data, namely AI-ColoWorkflow was compared against centre-specific and procedure-specific models on a held-out test set. The following metrics were used for evaluation: macro F1 score, balanced accuracy, precision, and recall. AI-ColoWorkflow achieved a macro F1 of 73.01% $\pm$ 10.27 (balanced accuracy 73.43%) for phase recognition and 39.82% $\pm$ 7.06 (balanced accuracy 38.65%) for step recognition. The global model outperformed centre- and procedure-specific models in most experiments except procedure-specific step recognition. In the generalization analysis, mean F1 was 48.42% for phase recognition. AI-ColoWorkflow can reliably recognize MIS-CRS phases. A single model trained on pooled, multicentric, multi-procedural data generalises at least as well as and often better than centre- or procedure-specific models for phase recognition in MIS-CRS, while procedure-specific step models retain advantages for certain procedure types, motivating hybrid training strategies for future surgical AI development.

AI.tldr: AI-ColoWorkflow is a deep learning model for automated surgical workflow analysis of minimally invasive colorectal surgeries (MIS-CRS). Combining a fine-tuned DINOv3 vision transformer with a hierarchical multi-stage temporal convolutional network, it achieves 73.01% macro F1 for phase recognition and 39.82% for step recognition. A single model trained on pooled multicentric data generalises at least as well as, and often better than, centre- or procedure-specific models for phase recognition.
AI.motivation: Manual video-based assessment (VBA) of MIS-CRS workflow using ColoWorkflow is time-consuming, limiting its implementation. An automated approach is needed to enable scalable surgical workflow analysis.
AI.method: Operative videos from 4 centres plus a public dataset were manually annotated for phases and steps per ColoWorkflow. A deep learning model combining a fine-tuned DINOv3 vision transformer (per-frame visual features) with a hierarchical multi-stage temporal convolutional network was jointly optimized for phase and step recognition. The pooled multicentric model (AI-ColoWorkflow) was compared against centre- and procedure-specific models on a held-out test set using macro F1, balanced accuracy, precision, and recall.
AI.result: AI-ColoWorkflow achieved macro F1 of 73.01% (balanced accuracy 73.43%) for phase recognition and 39.82% (balanced accuracy 38.65%) for step recognition. The global model outperformed centre- and procedure-specific models in most experiments except procedure-specific step recognition. Generalization analysis showed mean F1 of 48.42% for phase recognition.
AI.conclusion: AI-ColoWorkflow reliably recognises MIS-CRS phases. A single model trained on pooled multicentric, multi-procedural data generalises at least as well as or better than centre-/procedure-specific models for phase recognition, while procedure-specific step models retain advantages for certain procedures, motivating hybrid training strategies for future surgical AI development.

title: G3Ego: Gaze-Guided Graphs for Egocentric Action Understanding
comment: Accepted at the CONTEXTUS Workshop, ECCV 2026
summary:
Egocentric action understanding is often addressed using large video models pretrained on extensive exocentric datasets. However, many first-person actions depend on a small number of hand-object interactions involving only a few relevant entities.
  We propose G3Ego, a graph-based framework for egocentric action understanding that uses gaze as a structural cue to identify action-relevant entities in the scene. From sparsely sampled frames, G3Ego constructs action scene graphs from vision-language descriptions, grounded objects, and hand cues, and then prunes irrelevant entities using the camera wearer's gaze.
  The resulting graph embeddings are temporally aggregated for action recognition and anticipation. Unlike prior work that uses gaze primarily as an auxiliary modality or attention signal, G3Ego incorporates gaze directly into graph construction, producing efficient and interpretable representations focused on action-relevant interactions.
  Experiments on EGTEA Gaze+ and MECCANO show that G3Ego achieves competitive performance compared with video-based approaches and consistently improves Macro-F1 under class-imbalanced evaluation, while avoiding reliance on computationally expensive video pretraining. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of gaze-guided graph representations for egocentric action understanding.

AI.tldr: G3Ego is a graph-based framework for egocentric action understanding that leverages gaze as a structural cue to construct action scene graphs from sparsely sampled frames, pruning irrelevant entities and producing efficient, interpretable representations that achieve competitive performance on EGTEA Gaze+ and MECCANO without reliance on expensive video pretraining.
AI.motivation: Most egocentric action understanding relies on large video models pretrained on exocentric data, which is computationally expensive despite the fact that many first-person actions depend on only a small number of hand-object interactions with a few relevant entities.
AI.method: G3Ego builds action scene graphs from sparsely sampled frames using vision-language descriptions, grounded objects, and hand cues, then prunes irrelevant entities using the camera wearer's gaze. Gaze is incorporated directly into graph construction (rather than as an auxiliary modality), and resulting graph embeddings are temporally aggregated for action recognition and anticipation.
AI.result: G3Ego achieves competitive performance compared with video-based approaches on EGTEA Gaze+ and MECCANO, and consistently improves Macro-F1 under class-imbalanced evaluation while avoiding expensive video pretraining.
AI.conclusion: Gaze-guided graph representations are effective for egocentric action understanding, demonstrating that efficient and interpretable representations focused on action-relevant interactions can match video-based methods.

title: RoMAN-Flow: Taming Autoregressive Normalizing Flows for Offline Reinforcement Learning in Robotic Manipulation
summary: Offline reinforcement learning improves robotic policies using previously collected data without further environment interaction. Yet prevalent diffusion- and flow-matching robot policies lack tractable likelihoods, limiting their use in likelihood-based offline RL post-training. AR-NFs offer both expressive action modeling and exact likelihood evaluation, but their sequential sampling incurs substantial sampling overhead during policy optimization and deployment. We present RoMAN-Flow (Robotic Manipulation with Autoregressive Normalizing Flows), an offline reinforcement learning framework that makes AR-NF policies practical for robotic manipulation by addressing this sampling bottleneck in both stages. During policy optimization, RoMAN-Flow employs a sampling-free, advantage-weighted likelihood objective that assigns higher likelihood to high-advantage actions from the offline dataset without sampling from the autoregressive policy. For efficient deployment, it distills the optimized autoregressive policy into a one-step action generator, enabling low-latency action prediction. Experiments across multiple simulated manipulation benchmarks and real-world robotic platforms demonstrate that RoMAN-Flow achieves competitive policy performance while substantially reducing inference latency. Code is available at https://github.com/konnyaku28/RoMAN-Flow.

AI.tldr: RoMAN-Flow is an offline RL framework that makes autoregressive normalizing flow (AR-NF) policies practical for robotic manipulation by using a sampling-free advantage-weighted likelihood objective during optimization and distilling the policy into a one-step action generator for low-latency deployment.
AI.motivation: Diffusion- and flow-matching robot policies lack tractable likelihoods, limiting their use in likelihood-based offline RL post-training. AR-NFs offer both expressive action modeling and exact likelihood evaluation, but their sequential sampling incurs substantial overhead during both policy optimization and deployment.
AI.method: RoMAN-Flow employs (1) a sampling-free, advantage-weighted likelihood objective during policy optimization that assigns higher likelihood to high-advantage actions without sampling from the autoregressive policy, and (2) distillation of the optimized autoregressive policy into a one-step action generator for low-latency deployment.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple simulated manipulation benchmarks and real-world robotic platforms demonstrate that RoMAN-Flow achieves competitive policy performance while substantially reducing inference latency.
AI.conclusion: RoMAN-Flow makes AR-NF policies practical for offline RL in robotic manipulation by resolving the sampling bottleneck in both optimization and deployment stages, achieving competitive performance with much lower latency.

title: Unwarping the Lens: A Physics-Grounded Approach to Video Glasses Removal
summary: High-fidelity removal of eyeglasses from video is a major challenge in facial attribute editing, as the underlying facial geometry is often obscured by complex refractive distortions and view-dependent specular reflections. While large-scale generative priors have shown promise in eye-glasses removal via static image inpainting, they often lack the structural constraints necessary to maintain identity, expression, and pose, leading to visible "identity drift" in both static images and dynamic sequences. In this paper, we propose a novel transfer framework that addresses the stochastic nature of generative priors. Our pipeline first extracts high-fidelity synthetic face images from a commercial-grade generative model (Nano Banana, Gemini 3 Pro Image), regularizes them via a three-stage structural filtering process to preserve identity, expression, and pose, and finally applies physically-based simulation of lens optics during training to provide diverse, paired data. This process transfers Nano Banana's photo-realistic, multi-view knowledge into a specialized restoration architecture, JFSnet (Joint Feature-Spatial network). JFSnet integrates DINOv2-based semantic features with a convolutional decoder for spatial reconstruction, leveraging translation equivariance constraints to improve temporal consistency and high-frequency detail preservation. Evaluations on the curated Flickr-Faces-HQ (FFHQ) subset (12,163 images) show that our approach achieves high fidelity and structural accuracy, while maintaining inference speed of 27.68 FPS. In perceptual studies on CelebV-Text video sequences, our results are consistently preferred over diffusion and GAN-based baselines for ocular consistency, temporal stability, and overall restoration quality.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes JFSnet, a transfer framework for high-fidelity eyeglasses removal from video. It extracts synthetic face images from a commercial generative model (Nano Banana), regularizes them via three-stage structural filtering, and applies physically-based lens optics simulation for paired training data. The architecture integrates DINOv2 semantic features with a convolutional decoder, achieving 27.68 FPS and outperforming diffusion/GAN baselines in perceptual studies.
AI.motivation: Existing generative priors for eyeglasses removal lack structural constraints, causing identity drift in both static images and dynamic sequences. The reflective and refractive nature of eyeglasses obscures facial geometry, making high-fidelity removal in video particularly challenging.
AI.method: The pipeline: (1) extracts high-fidelity synthetic face images from Nano Banana (commercial generative model), (2) applies a three-stage structural filtering process to preserve identity/expression/pose, (3) uses physically-based lens optics simulation during training for diverse paired data, and (4) trains JFSnet, which integrates DINOv2 semantic features with a convolutional decoder under translation equivariance constraints for temporal consistency.
AI.result: On a curated FFHQ subset (12,163 images), the approach achieves high fidelity and structural accuracy at 27.68 FPS. Perceptual studies on CelebV-Text video sequences show consistent preference over diffusion and GAN baselines for ocular consistency, temporal stability, and overall restoration quality.
AI.conclusion: Transferring knowledge from large-scale generative priors into a specialized restoration architecture, combined with physical simulation of lens optics, effectively addresses identity drift and achieves efficient, high-quality eyeglasses removal in both still images and videos.

title: Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention for Hierarchical Feature Modulation toward Anatomy-Agnostic Segmentation
summary: Anatomically plausible segmentation remains challenging because of low contrast, ambiguous boundaries, and modality-specific artifacts. Interactive segmentation has emerged as a promising strategy to guide feature extraction and improve localization, particularly in structurally ambiguous regions. However, existing methods integrate prompts through late-stage fusion and lack explicit mechanisms for prompt-driven channel-wise modulation across hierarchical feature representations, limiting their ability to capture deeper contextual and modality-specific variations. To address these limitations, we introduce Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention (PCCA), a novel modulation mechanism that enables deep, hierarchical integration of semantic prompts within encoder-decoder networks. PCCA extracts compact channel descriptors via pooling, projects them into a shared space, and fuses them through a gated excitation mechanism to compute prompt-aware channel attention weights. These weights adaptively recalibrate feature responses across multiple network stages, enabling prompt-conditioned, semantically enriched hierarchical representations. Building on this, we propose PROMISE-Net, instantiated in two network variants: a convolutional model (PROMISE-CNN) and a transformer-based model (PROMISE-Txformer). Across the ISIC-Lesion, Kvasir-Polyp, CAMUS-Cardiac, and Kvasir-Instrument benchmarks, integrating PCCA into PROMISE-CNN yielded relative IoU gains of 10.4%, 8.7%, 0.8%, and 3.4%, respectively, over the baseline U-Net, while PROMISE-Txformer achieved corresponding gains of 7.6%, 23.0%, 2.1%, and 1.1%, respectively, over the baseline UNETR. These results show consistent improvements across architectures, imaging modalities, and anatomical targets, establishing PCCA and PROMISE-Net as a scalable, generalizable framework for prompt-aware hierarchical feature modulation in medical image segmentation.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention (PCCA), a mechanism for deep hierarchical integration of semantic prompts in medical image segmentation networks. The authors propose PROMISE-Net in two variants (CNN-based and transformer-based), which consistently outperform their respective baselines (U-Net and UNETR) across four medical imaging benchmarks spanning skin lesions, polyps, cardiac, and instrument segmentation.
AI.motivation: Anatomically plausible segmentation is challenging due to low contrast, ambiguous boundaries, and modality-specific artifacts. Existing interactive segmentation methods rely on late-stage fusion of prompts and lack explicit mechanisms for prompt-driven channel-wise modulation across hierarchical feature representations, limiting their ability to capture deep contextual and modality-specific variations.
AI.method: PCCA extracts compact channel descriptors via pooling, projects them into a shared space, and fuses them through a gated excitation mechanism to compute prompt-aware channel attention weights. These weights adaptively recalibrate feature responses across multiple network stages, enabling prompt-conditioned, semantically enriched hierarchical representations. Two network variants are proposed: PROMISE-CNN (convolutional) and PROMISE-Txformer (transformer-based).
AI.result: On ISIC-Lesion, Kvasir-Polyp, CAMUS-Cardiac, and Kvasir-Instrument benchmarks, PROMISE-CNN achieved relative IoU gains of 10.4%, 8.7%, 0.8%, and 3.4% over U-Net, while PROMISE-Txformer achieved gains of 7.6%, 23.0%, 2.1%, and 1.1% over UNETR.
AI.conclusion: PCCA and PROMISE-Net establish a scalable, generalizable framework for prompt-aware hierarchical feature modulation, showing consistent improvements across architectures, imaging modalities, and anatomical targets in medical image segmentation.

title: Ultra-High-Definition Restoration Transformers with Correlation Matching Transformation
summary: We propose UHDformer++, a general Transformer-based framework to solve numerous Ultra-High-Definition (UHD) image restoration tasks. UHDformer++ operates across $4$ coordinated learning spaces: 1) a high-resolution space (HR) for multi-level feature extraction, 2) a low-resolution space (LR) for learning compact, representative features, 3) a super-resolution space (SR) for upsampling low-resolution features from SR, and 4) a low-high fusion and reconstruction space (LHFR) for final image restoration. Specifically, HR extracts multi-scale high-resolution features and fuses them with low-resolution cues to produce residual images, while LR distills complementary representations from HR to improve restoration quality. To supply LHFR with richer features, SR super-resolves LR outputs before fusion. We further introduce two modules to bridge the high- and low-resolution spaces. The Feature-Refined Correlation Matching Transformation (FR-CMT) module selects the top $C/r~(C~\text{denotes the number of channels;~}r\geq1~\text{controls the squeezing level})$, from the fusion between max- and mean-pooled high-resolution features to replace less informative channels in the low-resolution Transformer. The Adaptive Channel Modulator (ACM) adaptively recalibrates multi-scale high-resolution features, ensuring that only task-relevant information propagates to LR. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UHDformer++ reduces model parameters by at least 86\% compared with recent state-of-the-art methods while achieving substantial performance gains across $5$ UHD restoration tasks, including low-light image enhancement, dehazing, deblurring, deraining, and desnowing. Code will be released at https://github.com/supersupercong/uhdformerplus.

AI.tldr: UHDformer++ is a Transformer-based framework for Ultra-High-Definition image restoration that operates across four coordinated learning spaces (HR, LR, SR, LHFR), introduces FR-CMT and ACM modules to bridge high- and low-resolution spaces, reduces parameters by 86% while improving performance across 5 restoration tasks.
AI.motivation: Ultra-High-Definition image restoration is challenging due to the massive computational cost and memory requirements of processing UHD images. Existing methods struggle to balance restoration quality with computational efficiency, motivating the need for a more efficient yet effective framework.
AI.method: UHDformer++ uses a four-space architecture: HR space for multi-level high-resolution feature extraction, LR space for compact feature learning, SR space for upsampling low-resolution features, and LHFR space for fusion and final reconstruction. Two novel modules bridge spaces: FR-CMT selects top informative channels from fused max/mean-pooled HR features to replace less informative channels in the LR Transformer, and ACM adaptively recalibrates multi-scale HR features to propagate only task-relevant information to LR.
AI.result: UHDformer++ reduces model parameters by at least 86% compared with recent state-of-the-art methods while achieving substantial performance gains across 5 UHD restoration tasks: low-light image enhancement, dehazing, deblurring, deraining, and desnowing.
AI.conclusion: The proposed UHDformer++ demonstrates that a coordinated multi-space learning approach with efficient feature selection and modulation can simultaneously achieve high restoration quality and dramatically reduced model complexity, offering a general and efficient solution for diverse UHD image restoration tasks.

title: Towards Surgical World-Action Modeling: A Preliminary Joint Visual-Trajectory Forecasting for Surgical Motion Planning
summary: Reliable surgical planning requires models to anticipate not only how instruments will move, but also how the operative visual state will evolve together with such motion. Existing approaches typically treat future scene generation and instrument trajectory prediction as two separate tasks. Scene-only models cannot directly evaluate the accuracy of future instrument motion at the trajectory level, while trajectory-only models fail to capture the visual consequences of instrument movement, leaving the consistency between predicted trajectories and future scene evolution unaddressed. Jointly forecasting both provides a more complete account of surgical action-scene dynamics by enabling explicit trajectory-level evaluation while simultaneously modeling the corresponding visual evolution. To bridge this gap, we present a preliminary joint visual-trajectory world-action model that simultaneously forecasts future visual states and instrument trajectories from historical surgical observations. Specifically, we encode historical video frames and tool trajectories into latent representations, which are processed by a temporal-spatial encoder and subsequently decoded through separate visual-state and trajectory prediction heads. Based on this preliminary architecture, a chunked autoregressive rollout is repeatedly applied to predict fifteen future steps. The chunked strategy consistently outperforms direct one-shot prediction across all evaluated horizons, improving first-segment PSNR from 18.86 to 23.11 dB and reducing ADE from 45.77 to 22.22 pixels. These results demonstrate the initial feasibility of joint visual-motion forecasting. However, we observe progressive visual degradation and accumulated trajectory errors over longer prediction horizons, which remain important challenges for future surgical world-action modeling.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a preliminary joint visual-trajectory world-action model for surgical scene forecasting that simultaneously predicts future visual states and instrument trajectories from historical observations. Using a chunked autoregressive rollout strategy, the model improves PSNR from 18.86 to 23.11 dB and reduces ADE from 45.77 to 22.22 pixels, demonstrating feasibility of joint forecasting while highlighting challenges of progressive degradation over longer horizons.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches treat future scene generation and instrument trajectory prediction as separate tasks, failing to capture the consistency between predicted trajectories and future scene evolution. A joint forecasting model is needed to provide a complete account of surgical action-scene dynamics with explicit trajectory-level evaluation and visual evolution modeling.
AI.method: A joint visual-trajectory world-action model encodes historical video frames and tool trajectories into latent representations, processes them through a temporal-spatial encoder, and decodes via separate visual-state and trajectory prediction heads. A chunked autoregressive rollout is applied for fifteen-step future prediction.
AI.result: The chunked strategy outperforms direct one-shot prediction across all horizons, improving first-segment PSNR from 18.86 to 23.11 dB and reducing ADE from 45.77 to 22.22 pixels. Progressive visual degradation and accumulated trajectory errors are observed over longer horizons.
AI.conclusion: Joint visual-motion forecasting is initially feasible for surgical planning, but challenges remain regarding progressive visual degradation and trajectory error accumulation over extended prediction horizons, motivating future work in surgical world-action modeling.

title: CalcSeg: Confidence-aware 3D Latent Context Curriculum Learning For Myocardial Scar Segmentation From Single-Stack LGE-CMRs
summary: Myocardial scar segmentation from single-stack late gadolinium-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (LGE-CMR) imaging has been a longstanding and clinically important challenge, particularly in the presence of low tissue contrast, diffuse, and small scar regions. These challenges are further intensified by the limited availability of 3D spatial context. This paper presents CalcSeg, a Confidence-aware latent context curriculum learning framework that leverages fused 3D feature representations from single-stack 2D LGE-CMR images for robust scar segmentation. Specifically, we introduce a dynamic semi-supervised curriculum learning strategy that progressively expands training from easier to more challenging scar cases using a learned confidence-aware scoring function. Such a function integrates errors in the predicted scar maps with quantified epistemic uncertainty and scar burden estimation to automatically assess sample difficulty without requiring manual labels. To compensate for the limited spatial context in single-stack acquisitions, we then develop a latent slice-wise self-attention to capture inter-slice dependencies and infer 3D spatial representations from sparse 2D inputs. We evaluate CalcSeg on multi-center clinical LGE-CMR datasets and benchmark against existing scar segmentation networks. Experimental results show that CalcSeg consistently outperforms all competing methods, particularly with substantial improvements on clinically challenging cases. Our code is released on Github.

AI.tldr: CalcSeg is a confidence-aware latent context curriculum learning framework for myocardial scar segmentation from single-stack 2D LGE-CMR images, using dynamic semi-supervised curriculum learning and latent slice-wise self-attention to overcome limited 3D spatial context and challenging low-contrast scar cases.
AI.motivation: Myocardial scar segmentation from single-stack LGE-CMR is challenging due to low tissue contrast, diffuse/small scar regions, and limited 3D spatial context, compounded by scarce annotated data.
AI.method: Introduces a dynamic semi-supervised curriculum learning strategy that progressively trains from easy to hard cases using a confidence-aware scoring function (integrating prediction errors, epistemic uncertainty, and scar burden). A latent slice-wise self-attention mechanism captures inter-slice dependencies to infer 3D spatial representations from sparse 2D inputs.
AI.result: Evaluated on multi-center clinical LGE-CMR datasets, CalcSeg consistently outperforms existing scar segmentation networks, with substantial improvements on clinically challenging cases.
AI.conclusion: CalcSeg demonstrates that combining confidence-aware curriculum learning with latent 3D context modeling effectively addresses robust scar segmentation under limited data and spatial context constraints.

title: DreamHand: Repurposing Video Diffusion Models for Occlusion-Robust Egocentric 3D Hand Motion Recovery
summary: Egocentric video offers scalable manipulation data for embodied AI, yet recovering metric 3D hand trajectories remains challenging due to severe object occlusion and frequent out-of-sight gaps. Existing single-frame and windowed temporal regressors fail when hand shortly leaves the frame, while recent video diffusion models (VDMs) rely on heavy, stochastic multi-step sampling as pixel-space renderers. We instead repurpose VDM into a deterministic geometry encoder. A single forward pass over the clean latent exposes scene content beyond current observations, including occluded and out-of-sight hands. We introduce DreamHand, an offline clip-level framework that extracts features via a Deterministic Clean-Latent Encoder and decodes them with a Bidirectional Spatiotemporal Decoder. DreamHand recovers continuous bimanual trajectories with metric placement and no external detector, while a Ray-Based Camera Solver supports a second configuration that needs no test-time camera intrinsics. Across five egocentric benchmarks, DreamHand sets a new state of the art, cutting MPJPE-p by 30% on occlusion-heavy ARCTIC and 40% on HOT3D. These gains reach 46%-61% once out-of-sight hands are included in the evaluation, offering a scalable path from everyday human video to robot manipulation data.

AI.tldr: DreamHand repurposes a video diffusion model into a deterministic geometry encoder to recover metric 3D hand trajectories from egocentric video, handling occlusion and out-of-sight gaps, achieving state-of-the-art results (30-46% error reduction) across five benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing single-frame and windowed temporal regressors fail when hands briefly leave the frame or are occluded, while video diffusion models are heavy and rely on stochastic multi-step sampling as pixel-space renderers—there is a need for an efficient approach that can reason beyond current observations.
AI.method: DreamHand converts a video diffusion model into a deterministic geometry encoder via a single forward pass over clean latents, exposing scene content beyond current observations. An offline clip-level framework extracts features with a Deterministic Clean-Latent Encoder and decodes them via a Bidirectional Spatiotemporal Decoder, recovering continuous bimanual trajectories with metric placement and no external detector. A Ray-Based Camera Solver supports a no-test-time-intrinsics configuration.
AI.result: Across five egocentric benchmarks, DreamHand sets a new state of the art, cutting MPJPE-p by 30% on occlusion-heavy ARCTIC and 40% on HOT3D, with gains reaching 46%-61% when out-of-sight hands are included.
AI.conclusion: DreamHand offers a scalable path from everyday human video to robot manipulation data by efficiently recovering metric hand trajectories despite severe occlusion and out-of-sight gaps, without requiring external detectors or test-time camera intrinsics.

title: Inter-X++: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Human-Human Interaction Analysis
summary: The capability to perceive and synthesize human-human interactions is fundamental to developing intelligent digital human systems. However, existing datasets and modeling approaches are fundamentally constrained by low-fidelity kinematics, the omission of dexterous hand gestures and a severe lack of rich multimodal annotations. Furthermore, fragmented interaction representations and inconsistent evaluation protocols also impede fair and rigorous benchmarking. To systematically address these bottlenecks, we present Inter-X++, a comprehensive and large-scale benchmark designed to empower versatile HHI analysis. Captured via a novel hybrid motion capture system, Inter-X++ provides 11,388 high-fidelity interaction sequences and over 8.1M frames, featuring precise whole-body movements and detailed finger articulations. Meanwhile, we enrich the data foundation with multifaceted annotations, including hierarchical fine-grained textual descriptions, interaction categories, causal interaction orders, the relationship and personality of the subjects, as well as vertex-level contact maps and physically regularized constraints. Leveraging these elaborate annotations, we formulate a unified testing ground comprising four categories of downstream tasks that symmetrically span both generative and perceptive paradigms. To eliminate benchmarking ambiguities, we systematically standardize the interaction representations and evaluation protocols. Finally, we go beyond dataset construction to propose OpenHHI, a single and unified HHI representation and modeling framework that jointly optimizes interaction reconstruction and semantic understanding. Extensive experiments reveal that OpenHHI achieves state-of-the-art performance on both generation and perception tasks. This definitively proves that our unified representation successfully bridges interaction understanding and generation simultaneously.

AI.tldr: Inter-X++ is a large-scale benchmark for human-human interaction (HHI) analysis, providing 11,388 high-fidelity interaction sequences with over 8.1M frames captured via a novel hybrid motion capture system. It includes rich multimodal annotations (textual descriptions, interaction categories, causal orders, subject relationships/personality, contact maps) and defines four standardized downstream tasks spanning generative and perceptive paradigms. The paper also proposes OpenHHI, a unified HHI representation and modeling framework that jointly optimizes interaction reconstruction and semantic understanding, achieving state-of-the-art performance on both generation and perception tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing HHI datasets and modeling approaches suffer from low-fidelity kinematics, missing dexterous hand gesture modeling, lack of rich multimodal annotations, fragmented interaction representations, and inconsistent evaluation protocols—all of which impede fair and rigorous benchmarking of human-human interaction understanding and synthesis.
AI.method: The authors construct Inter-X++, a comprehensive benchmark captured via a hybrid motion capture system, with precise whole-body and finger articulation data. They enrich it with multifaceted annotations (hierarchical text descriptions, interaction categories, causal orders, subject traits, contact maps, and physical constraints) and standardize interaction representations and evaluation protocols across four downstream task categories. They further introduce OpenHHI, a unified representation and modeling framework that jointly optimizes interaction reconstruction and semantic understanding.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that OpenHHI achieves state-of-the-art performance on both generation and perception tasks, demonstrating that the unified representation successfully bridges interaction understanding and generation.
AI.conclusion: The unified HHI representation in OpenHHI effectively bridges interaction understanding and generation, and Inter-X++ provides a comprehensive, standardized benchmark to advance human-human interaction analysis.

title: Swift-Image: Exploring the Performance Frontier of Compact Unified Image Generation Models
summary: We present Swift-Image, a compact unified model for text-to-image generation, single-image editing, and multi-image editing. Our goal is to explore how far a relatively small visual generator can be pushed through systematic training engineering under a constrained computational budget. Swift-Image adopts an efficient 6B single-stream DiT and a progressive training pipeline that evolves from broad semantic coverage to higher resolution, stronger visual quality, and unified generation-editing supervision. For post-training, we employ parallel expert reinforcement learning followed by multi-teacher on-policy distillation to alleviate interference among heterogeneous objectives. We further decouple high-level reasoning from pixel-level rendering with a Prompt Enhancer that translates user requests into generator-aligned visual specifications. For efficient deployment, structural pruning and few-step distillation produce 3B and accelerated variants. Swift-Image achieves leading aggregate performance among evaluated open-source models with only 6B parameters and 243K GPU training hours; the compressed 3B model incurs nearly no loss, while few-step distillation further improves aggregate editing performance with substantially fewer sampling steps. Our study also summarizes practical lessons for architecture, data curriculum, post-training, prompt enhancement, and model compression.

AI.tldr: Swift-Image is a compact 6B-parameter unified model for text-to-image generation and editing, trained with systematic engineering under constrained compute. It achieves leading performance among open-source models via progressive training, expert RL, multi-teacher distillation, a Prompt Enhancer for decoupling reasoning from rendering, and compression to 3B with minimal loss.
AI.motivation: To explore how far a relatively small visual generator can be pushed through systematic training engineering under a constrained computational budget, while unified text-to-image generation and multi-image editing remain challenging for compact models.
AI.method: Swift-Image uses an efficient 6B single-stream DiT with a progressive training pipeline (from semantic coverage to resolution, quality, and unified supervision). Post-training employs parallel expert RL followed by multi-teacher on-policy distillation to handle heterogeneous objectives. A Prompt Enhancer decouples high-level reasoning from pixel rendering. Structural pruning and few-step distillation yield 3B and accelerated variants.
AI.result: Swift-Image achieves leading aggregate performance among open-source models with only 6B parameters and 243K GPU training hours. The compressed 3B model incurs nearly no loss, and few-step distillation improves aggregate editing performance with substantially fewer sampling steps.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides practical lessons for architecture, data curriculum, post-training, prompt enhancement, and model compression, demonstrating that compact models can compete with larger ones through careful training engineering.

title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video
summary: We present 4DAnyone, a framework for reconstructing 4D humans from an uncalibrated monocular video by generating reconstruction-grade multiview-consistent videos and lifting them into 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS). Existing camera-controlled video diffusion models synthesize plausible novel-view videos but fail to maintain consistency when scaled to the tens of target views required for 4DGS reconstruction. We identify this failure as a bounded-attention-context problem: when target views exceed the capacity of a single DiT forward pass, they must be split into groups, exposing two coupled bottlenecks. On the reference-context side, conditioning on all previously generated views grows as $O(N)$, weakening cross-view appearance guidance. On the target-context side, disjoint groups cannot directly exchange information, causing global structural drift. 4DAnyone addresses both bottlenecks with two complementary designs: Reference Context Packing (RCP) compresses growing reference views into a fixed-length mixed-resolution context with $O(1)$ reference-context complexity, while Target Context Routing (TCR) rotates target-view groupings during denoising to share context across groups at high-noise steps and stabilize details at low-noise steps. We further build the MVGameHuman dataset using our in-house game engine and combine it with light-stage and in-the-wild video datasets for training. Experiments on DNA-Rendering and DyMVHumans show that 4DAnyone outperforms prior methods in both novel-view video quality and downstream 4DGS reconstruction, with robust in-the-wild generalization. See our project page for video results and source code: https://4danyone.github.io.

AI.tldr: 4DAnyone reconstructs 4D humans from monocular video by generating multiview-consistent videos via video diffusion and lifting them into 4D Gaussian Splatting, addressing the bounded-attention-context problem with Reference Context Packing and Target Context Routing.
AI.motivation: Existing camera-controlled video diffusion models cannot maintain consistency when generating the tens of target views required for 4DGS reconstruction, because target views exceed the single DiT forward pass capacity and must be split into groups, causing cross-view appearance degradation and global structural drift.
AI.method: 4DAnyone introduces two complementary designs: (1) Reference Context Packing (RCP) compresses growing reference views into a fixed-length mixed-resolution context with O(1) reference-context complexity; (2) Target Context Routing (TCR) rotates target-view groupings during denoising to share context across groups at high-noise steps and stabilize details at low-noise steps. Training uses the MVGameHuman dataset (built with an in-house game engine) combined with light-stage and in-the-wild video datasets.
AI.result: Experiments on DNA-Rendering and DyMVHumans show 4DAnyone outperforms prior methods in both novel-view video quality and downstream 4DGS reconstruction, with robust in-the-wild generalization.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively solves multiview consistency scaling for 4D human reconstruction from monocular video, achieving state-of-the-art results and generalization to in-the-wild scenarios.

title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
comment: Project Page: doby-xu.github.io/WithEveryone/ ;Code will be released: github.com/Doby-Xu/WithEveryone/
summary: Identity-preserving image generation becomes increasingly unreliable when a scene must contain many specified people. Beyond retaining each identity, the model must bind every reference to a distinct person and location, while training-time identity losses must establish correspondence among several noisy predicted faces. We introduce WithEveryone, a unified framework for generating group images up to ten reference identities. WithEveryone injects each selected identity as an addressed token, predicts a structured identity--layout plan, and renders the plan as a visual condition. Its key objective, Layout-Grounded ID Loss, uses annotated face regions to supervise the intended identities directly, avoiding unstable embedding-based face matching; ID Representation Forcing additionally trains a prediction for each identity before image synthesis. On an identity-disjoint benchmark, WithEveryone achieves the highest target-context identity similarity, improving face similarity from 0.462 for GPT-Image-2 to 0.499, while reducing copy-paste artifacts from 0.169 to 0.055. It further covers 97.3\% of the requested identities with a duplicate rate of only 2.8\%. These results show that explicit identity--layout grounding enables identity-preserving generation to scale to larger groups without relying on direct reference-face copying.

AI.tldr: WithEveryone is a unified framework for identity-preserving group image generation that scales to up to ten reference identities by injecting addressed tokens, predicting an identity-layout plan, and using Layout-Grounded ID Loss with ID Representation Forcing to supervise intended identities through annotated face regions.
AI.motivation: Identity-preserving image generation becomes increasingly unreliable when a scene must contain many specified people, because the model must bind every reference identity to a distinct person and location while establishing correspondence among several noisy predicted faces during training.
AI.method: WithEveryone injects each selected identity as an addressed token, predicts a structured identity-layout plan, and renders the plan as a visual condition. The key objective, Layout-Grounded ID Loss, uses annotated face regions to supervise intended identities directly (avoiding unstable embedding-based face matching). Additionally, ID Representation Forcing trains a prediction for each identity before image synthesis.
AI.result: On an identity-disjoint benchmark, WithEveryone achieves the highest target-context identity similarity, improving face similarity from 0.462 (GPT-Image-2) to 0.499, reducing copy-paste artifacts from 0.169 to 0.055, covering 97.3% of requested identities with a duplicate rate of only 2.8%.
AI.conclusion: Explicit identity-layout grounding enables identity-preserving generation to scale to larger groups without relying on direct reference-face copying.
